rationale: Both candidates are near-clone UKB snpnet scores from the same pan-trait framework paper with identical covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and similar ancestry setup, so the decision rests on endpoint fidelity and PRS-only metrics. PGS001262 uses a direct doctor-diagnosed angina phenotype (“Vascular/heart problems diagnosed by doctor Angina”), which is a cleaner generic disease-status endpoint for the target trait than PGS001261’s time-to-event (TTE) formulation. Performance is also slightly better for PGS001262 on PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.58683 vs 0.58233; PGS-only R² 0.01304 vs 0.01228), with both remaining plausible relative to the heritability ceiling. Differences are small, hence moderate confidence, but PGS001262 has the edge on both phenotype alignment and PRS-only performance.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (same trait_reported/trait_efo). However, PGS000753 uses a narrower endpoint (“Prevalent abdominal aortic aneurysm”) and a very sparse P+T score (29 variants) with only a moderate OR=1.37 per SD and no PRS-comparable AUC/R2 reported. PGS003973 is from a large multi-cohort AAA GWAS meta-analysis context, uses genome-wide shrinkage (PRS-CS) with ~1.1M variants (stronger structural capture of polygenic signal), and reports discrimination (C-index 0.882) with only basic covariates (age, age^2, sex)—though this is a full-model metric and not PRS-only. Given the absence of PRS-only metrics for both, the stronger method/variant coverage and disease-focused multi-cohort development support PGS003973 over the sparse prevalent-only PGS000753.

PGS001267 is the better match to the target trait as a generic ankylosing spondylitis PRS: its trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are direct disease status (“Ankylosing spondylitis”), whereas PGS001268 is explicitly a time-to-event/incident-style endpoint (“Ankylosing spondylitis (time-to-event)”, phenotyping_reported “TTE ankylosing spondylitis”), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic disease target. Both are otherwise near-clones (same pan-trait UKB framework paper, same snpnet method, 10 variants, same training N, same covariates, same ancestry distribution and validation size). Although PGS001268 has slightly higher PRS-only AUROC/R2 (0.7346/0.1023 vs 0.7265/0.0988), the difference is small and does not outweigh the cleaner endpoint alignment of PGS001267.

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.539 and PGS-only R²=0.00291 (and incremental AUROC), with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and multi-ancestry evaluation listed, allowing a heritability-ceiling sanity check. PGS004477 has a more specific ICD10-like endpoint label (“M13 Other arthritis”) and a genome-wide LDpred2 build with an OR=1.20, but it provides no AUROC/R² (all null) and covariates are unknown, making its predictive performance and comparability much less verifiable from the visible fields.

Both candidates map cleanly to angina pectoris (same trait_efo). However, PGS001261 provides PRS-comparable performance evidence (PGS-only AUROC=0.58233 and PGS-only R2=0.01228) with basic covariates and a time-to-event angina endpoint; its PRS-only R2 is also plausible relative to the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.009–0.014). In contrast, PGS005052 lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 entirely (only a full-model C-index=0.766 and an OR=1.491), making its discrimination evidence less directly comparable for PRS quality judging; its training sample size is also not reported. While PGS005052 has a phecode-defined endpoint and multi-ancestry context, the missing PRS-only metrics are a decisive evidence gap versus PGS001261’s explicit PRS-only reporting.

PGS004913 has cleaner endpoint fidelity to the target: both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis,” matching the alcoholic liver cirrhosis concept, whereas PGS001777’s phenotyping_reported is “Cirrhosis (males),” a broader/sex-restricted phenotype that is less directly aligned. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS001777’s reported AUROC=0.671 is a full-model metric and not comparable as PRS evidence; by contrast PGS004913 at least reports a PRS-linked effect size (OR top vs bottom deciles 4.4) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), suggesting less risk of clinical packaging. Both are EUR-only, but overall PGS004913 is the better-supported direct-match PRS for alcohol-associated cirrhosis given the phenotype alignment and cleaner covariate disclosure.

PGS005254 is the better-supported match to the target trait aortic stenosis: it has exact trait alignment in both trait_reported and trait_efo ("Aortic stenosis" / "aortic stenosis"), whereas PGS005255 is primarily a related quantitative trait (trait_reported "Mean pressure gradient"; trait_efo includes "aortic measurement"), making it less endpoint-faithful despite sharing the same phenotyping_reported (incident aortic stenosis). Both candidates are otherwise near-clones (same publication, PRS-CS, EUR-only dev/eval, identical covariates, same validation N), so the decision falls to endpoint fidelity and available effect-size evidence; PGS005254 also shows a slightly stronger HR per SD (1.64 vs 1.53).

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo aortic stenosis; incident aortic stenosis phenotyping; EUR-only dev/eval). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on effect-size evidence and comparability. PGS005254 provides a clear per-SD HR with CI (HR=1.64, 1.50–1.78) under relatively basic covariates (age, age^2, sex, PCs), making the genetic contribution easier to interpret. PGS005252’s only discrimination-like metric is a full-model C-index=0.87 alongside a very heavy clinical covariate set (multiple comorbidities and BMI/smoking/renal failure), which is likely covariate-driven and not comparable as PRS evidence; its HR=1.92 is reported without CI. Despite PGS005252’s larger validation N and slightly higher HR point estimate, the cleaner covariate design and better-specified effect-size reporting make PGS005254 better-supported on the visible fields.

PGS001135 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.539) and PGS-only R2 (0.00291) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array), allowing a clean sanity check against the arthritis heritability ceiling and indicating the PRS contribution is small but quantified. It also has broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS) than PGS004547. In contrast, PGS004547 has no AUC/R2 (only an OR=1.26, suggesting weak-to-moderate signal) and unknown covariates, making its predictive performance and comparability harder to judge despite its larger variant count and more specific ICD10-style label (M13 other arthritis).

Both candidates have exact endpoint alignment to ankylosing spondylitis (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match) and use only basic demographic/PC-style covariates. However, PGS001267 provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R2=0.0988 in Europeans), whereas PGS002089 reports only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919) and has no PGS-only AUC/R2, making its predictive evidence less directly comparable. Although PGS002089 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with many more variants (22,026 vs 10) and includes some non-EUR evaluation (EUR/GME/SAS), the lack of standard PRS-only discrimination metrics on the record leaves it less well-supported than PGS001267 for this head-to-head.

Both candidates have good endpoint fidelity to the target (trait_efo=alcohol dependence; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on effect-size evidence and structural signals. PGS002738 is a genome-wide PRS-CS score with far broader variant coverage (326,000 variants) and shows a stronger reported discrimination proxy (OR top 10% vs rest 1.96 [1.54–2.51]) than PGS002739 (OR 1.76 [1.32–2.34]), suggesting better stratification. PGS002739 is a much sparser gene-based PRS-CSx model (858 variants) evaluated only in African American samples, which is valuable for AFR-specific use but provides weaker overall PRS signal on the visible metrics. With covariates unknown for both and similar validation sizes, the stronger OR and genome-wide construction favor PGS002738.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported = abdominal aortic aneurysm), same method (PRS-CS), same variant count (1,118,997), and same evaluation ancestry (EUR only), so endpoint fidelity and structural properties do not differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (pgs_only_* are null), so the only performance evidence is full-model discrimination, which is secondary and not directly comparable to PRS-only performance. Given that limitation, PGS003973 has cleaner disclosed covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) and reports a higher full-model time-to-event metric (C-index 0.882 with CI) versus PGS003972’s AUROC 0.69 with covariates unknown; validation sizes are similar (7,517 vs 6,940) and not decisive. Because the key PRS-comparable metrics are missing for both and the full-model metrics differ in type (C-index vs AUROC), confidence remains low despite selecting PGS003973.

Both candidates match the target trait well (same trait_reported/trait_efo), but PGS003972 has stronger structural and study-support signals: it is a genome-wide PRS-CS score with ~1.1M variants developed from a large multi-cohort AAA GWAS meta-analysis (many contributing cohorts listed), whereas PGS000753 is a sparse P+T score with only 29 variants and a smaller, more limited development context. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS003972’s full-model AUROC=0.69 cannot be treated as PRS-comparable; however PGS000753’s only comparable performance evidence is a moderate OR=1.37 per SD, which does not outweigh the much stronger method/coverage and broader disease-focused meta-analytic backing of PGS003972. Covariates are basic/known for PGS000753 (age/sex/PCs) but unknown for PGS003972; this lowers confidence but is not enough to offset the large gap in model structure and development evidence.

Both candidates map cleanly to the target (trait_efo = alcoholic liver cirrhosis). PGS000704 has a more faithful phenotype label (phenotyping_reported = "Alcoholic cirrhosis") and larger-scale genome-wide construction (183,271 variants; UKB dev n=223,327) with only basic covariates, but its reported performance is a full-model time-to-event C-index (0.711) with no PRS-only metrics, so the apparent edge is not clearly attributable to the PRS. PGS001777 is more disease-focused (publication explicitly about alcohol-related cirrhosis risk in drinkers) and provides stronger PRS-discrimination evidence via effect sizes (OR top 20% vs bottom 20% = 6.18; β=1.132) despite having only 3 variants and a smaller validation (n=1,390) and a slightly phenotype-restricted endpoint ("Cirrhosis (males)"). With no PRS-only AUC/R2 for either, the stronger PRS-specific effect-size evidence in PGS001777 outweighs PGS000704’s framework-style origin and non-PRS-comparable metric advantage.

PGS001268 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.7346 and PGS-only R²=0.10232 (plus CIs for AUROC), whereas PGS002089 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0919) and has no PRS-only AUC/R², making its predictive evidence less directly comparable. Endpoint fidelity slightly favors PGS002089 (direct ankylosing spondylitis) over PGS001268’s time-to-event (TTE) phenotype, but this mismatch is modest and not horizon-packaged. Both are UKB-based framework-style scores; however, PGS002089’s portability framing and missing PRS-only metrics leave weaker visible support than PGS001268’s cleaner PRS-only metric reporting. Covariates are basic in both, so they don’t differentiate strongly.

PGS002739 is the better-supported match to the target trait alcohol dependence because its endpoint is directly aligned across fields (trait_reported: "Alcohol use disorder", trait_efo: "alcohol dependence", phenotyping_reported: "Alcohol use disorder"), whereas PGS000201 is more indirect (trait_reported: "Problematic alcohol use" and trait_efo: "alcohol dependence measurement" despite an AUD DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype). On performance evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS002739 provides a clear case-control discrimination signal (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.76), while PGS000201 only reports a small incremental ΔR² vs covariates (0.01192) and a beta without an interpretable risk contrast. PGS000201 has cleaner disclosed covariates and far broader genome-wide coverage (1,094,954 variants) than the sparse gene-based 858-variant PGS002739, but the stronger endpoint fidelity plus a more directly interpretable risk stratification metric in PGS002739 outweigh those advantages here; confidence is moderate due to missing covariate details for PGS002739 and non-comparable metric types.

Both candidates map cleanly to angina pectoris (same trait_efo), but PGS001262 provides directly comparable PRS-only performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.58683; PGS-only R2=0.01304) with basic covariates and these are sanity-consistent with the trait’s low observed h2 (~0.009–0.014). In contrast, PGS005052 lacks PRS-comparable metrics entirely (auc/r2/pgs_only_* are null) and only reports a full-model C-index (0.766) plus an OR=1.491, making its discrimination evidence less directly comparable for PRS ranking. While PGS005052 has a more disease-focused phecode endpoint and a genome-wide score with broader GWAS ancestry, the absence of PRS-only AUC/R2 means its apparent performance cannot be fairly weighed against PGS001262’s explicit PRS-only metrics, so PGS001262 is better-supported on the visible fields.

PGS004913 is more endpoint-faithful and disease-focused for the target: its trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are explicitly “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis,” matching the target concept (alcoholic liver cirrhosis) without being embedded in a broad pan-trait/biomarker framework. It also provides a strong PRS-stratification effect size (OR top vs bottom deciles = 4.4), which is more directly interpretable as PRS signal than PGS000704’s reported full-model C-index (0.711), which is not PRS-only and cannot be substituted for PRS discrimination. PGS000704 has much larger training/validation and more variants, but it comes from a broad UKB biomarker genetics paper and only reports an HR=1.18 (modest) alongside a covariate-adjusted time-to-event metric, leaving weaker standalone PRS evidence. With both lacking PRS-only AUC/R2, the cleaner endpoint focus and stronger effect-size evidence favor PGS004913.

PGS005252 is the better-supported match to the target trait (aortic stenosis) because its trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are directly aligned to incident aortic stenosis, whereas PGS005255 is reported as “Mean pressure gradient” with trait_efo including “aortic measurement,” making it more of a valve-function/measurement score despite also mentioning incident AS. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model C-index=0.87 in PGS005252 is not treated as PRS-comparable; however, PGS005252 shows a stronger per-SD effect size (HR=1.92 vs 1.53 for PGS005255), which is meaningful discrimination evidence when PRS-only metrics are absent. PGS005252 does use heavier clinical covariates (multiple comorbidities and BMI/smoking/renal failure) than PGS005255’s basic age/sex/PC adjustment, which tempers confidence, but overall endpoint fidelity plus stronger HR favors PGS005252.

PGS002738 is the better match to the target trait alcohol dependence on endpoint fidelity: its trait_efo is exactly alcohol dependence and both trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are Alcohol use disorder (a direct clinical diagnosis closely aligned to dependence). PGS000201 is more weakly aligned conceptually (trait_reported is Problematic alcohol use; trait_efo is alcohol dependence measurement) and its phenotype is a DSM-5 criteria count (log-transformed), which is more of a severity/measurement construct than a straightforward dependence case-control endpoint. Neither record provides clean PRS-only AUC/R2, but PGS002738 at least shows a reasonably strong risk stratification effect (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96), whereas PGS000201’s only PRS-comparable metric is a small incremental ΔR²=0.01192. Covariates in PGS000201 are basic (age/sex/PCs/array/site) and not a major penalty, but PGS002738’s stronger endpoint match and effect-size evidence outweigh PGS000201’s modest ΔR² and larger SNP count.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same reported phenotype (M13 Other arthritis), same EFO mapping (arthritis), same training cohort (UKB), identical training/validation sizes and EUR-only DEV/EVAL, and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 with covariates listed as Unknown. With metrics missing, the main differentiators are structural method signals and available effect size. PGS004547 uses an explicit multi-score aggregation/metaPRS approach (RFDiseasemetaPRS), which is a positive structural signal versus the single-score LDpred2 in PGS004477, and it also shows a higher per-SD OR (1.262 vs 1.196), indicating stronger PRS discrimination on the visible record. Given otherwise identical metadata, PGS004547 is better supported.

PGS001344 is better-supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.64568 and PGS-only R2=0.05973 (no covariates), which can be sanity-checked against asthma h2_liability (~0.15) and are interpretable as standalone PRS metrics. In contrast, PGS002727 lacks PRS-only AUC/R2 and only shows full-model AUROC=0.66 and R2=0.04, which the guidance says should not be substituted for PRS-only performance; its OR=1.57 is supportive but not directly comparable to the missing PRS-only metrics. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (asthma; PGS002727 is pediatric-specific while PGS001344 is doctor-diagnosed general asthma), and while PGS002727 is disease-focused and multi-ancestry evaluated, the absence of PRS-only metrics makes its evidence package less clean than PGS001344’s explicit PRS-only reporting.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is not directly comparable as a PRS metric. However, PGS005168’s reported discrimination is explicitly packaged with a named clinical risk calculator covariate (CHARGE-AF) in addition to demographics/array, making its high C-index (0.8718) likely covariate-driven and less informative for standalone PRS quality. PGS002814 uses only basic covariates (age, sex, top 20 PCs), avoiding that risk-wrapper leakage, and it provides a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.94) as supportive PRS signal. Despite being evaluated only in East Asians and having fewer variants, the cleaner covariate design and strong OR make PGS002814 better-supported on the visible fields than the CHARGE-AF–augmented PGS005168.

Both candidates match the target trait well at the concept level (trait_reported and trait_efo are asthma). However, PGS002727 is explicitly a restricted endpoint (phenotyping_reported: pediatric asthma), which is a weaker match for generic asthma risk than PGS001782’s general “Asthma” phenotype. On PRS-comparable performance, PGS001782 reports a clear PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R²=0.048844 (and AUROC 0.659 with basic covariates sex/age/PCs), which is interpretable and below the asthma heritability ceiling; PGS002727 lacks any PGS-only AUC/R² and only shows full-model AUROC=0.66 and R²=0.04, which are not comparable as standalone PRS metrics. Although PGS002727 has broader multi-ancestry evaluation and a strong OR=1.57, the endpoint restriction plus missing PRS-only metrics makes it less well-supported overall than PGS001782.

PGS004587 is the better-supported match to the target trait (atopic eczema) because its endpoint is a generic incident atopic dermatitis/eczema phenotype (trait_reported: Atopic dermatitis; phenotyping_reported: Incident atopic dermatitis) aligned to the broad target, whereas PGS001773 is explicitly restricted to a subtype (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported: moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis), which is a narrower endpoint mismatch for a generic atopic eczema target. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2; PGS001773 reports only full-model AUROC/R² (0.93/0.49) with covariates including parental ethnicity, which is not PRS-comparable and is also implausibly high relative to the eczema heritability ceiling, so it cannot be used as strong PRS evidence. PGS004587 at least provides a PRS-stratified effect size (HR 1.153 high vs low PRS) and is evaluated in a large EUR cohort (n=337,910), while PGS001773 has much smaller validation (n=676) and no PRS-isolated metric.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_efo=atopic eczema; incident atopic dermatitis endpoint) and have identical evaluation ancestry (EUR) and validation sample size (n=337,910) with similarly light covariates. Neither reports PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so selection falls back to structural signals and effect size. PGS002755 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants, which is generally better suited to a polygenic trait like atopic eczema than PGS004587’s 23 genome-wide significant SNP score; it also shows a slightly stronger HR high-vs-low (1.249 vs 1.153). PGS004587’s listed multi-cohort training sources are supportive but don’t outweigh the much sparser construction and weaker HR given the lack of PRS-only metrics.

Both candidates target the correct disease concept (trait_efo includes atrial flutter; trait_reported is atrial fibrillation and flutter). However, PGS001339 provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.613 and PGS-only R2=0.02447) with basic covariates and these are sanity-consistent with the provided heritability ceiling guidance, whereas PGS002050 lacks PRS-only AUROC/R2 entirely and reports only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.1034), which is less directly comparable for PRS discrimination. Although PGS002050 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with far more variants and slightly larger training N, the missing PRS-comparable metrics make it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001339.

Both candidates align well to the target trait (asthma) with direct diagnosis-style phenotyping, but PGS001782 is supported by a stronger study/transportability context and cleaner PRS-comparable metric framing. PGS001782 comes from a global multi-biobank analysis (many training/development cohorts listed) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto) with very large variant coverage (884,043), which is structurally favorable for a polygenic disease; it reports a PRS-comparable Nagelkerke R2 with covariates regressed out (0.048844), which is directly interpretable as PRS signal. PGS001344 reports explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 (0.64568/0.05973) and has broader evaluation ancestries, but it is from the known pan-trait UKB sparse-score framework (“across 813 traits”) with a very sparse model (6,139 variants) and single-biobank development, a pattern that domain guidance flags as less reliable for external generalization. Net: despite slightly higher reported PGS-only R2 for PGS001344, the framework+sparse-model penalty and stronger genome-wide multi-cohort evidence favor PGS001782.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC differences (0.78 for PGS005313 vs 0.74 for PGS002814) are not decisive and are not directly comparable. The stronger support for PGS005313 comes from structural/transportability signals: it uses a genome-wide cross-ancestry shrinkage approach (PRS-CSx) with ~1.27M variants and is evaluated across multiple ancestries, whereas PGS002814 is a sparse P+T score with 4,520 variants evaluated only in East Asians. Both have only basic covariates (age/sex; PGS002814 adds PCs), so no major leakage advantage either way. Given the lack of PRS-only metrics, the more genome-wide, cross-ancestry model with broader evaluation (PGS005313) is better-supported overall than the EAS-only sparse P+T model (PGS002814).

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (basal cell carcinoma), same publication, same EUR-only ancestry distribution, same training cohort (MGI) and training N (11,734), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same validation N (11,322). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC (0.632) is not a strong differentiator. The only visible edge is slightly better performance for PGS000454: marginally higher Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0489 vs 0.0487) and higher top-1% vs rest OR (3.79 vs 3.61) with essentially identical per-SD OR. Given the tiny differences and lack of PRS-only metrics, confidence is low, but PGS000454 is modestly better-supported on the reported validation outputs.

Both candidates match the target trait cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUCs are not directly comparable as PRS metrics. PGS005168 is strongly penalized for explicit clinical risk-calculator packaging via covariates including CHARGE-AF (plus age/age^2/sex/array), making its very high C-index=0.8718 likely covariate-driven and less informative about standalone PRS quality. PGS005313 uses only basic covariates (age, sex) and provides a strong PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.82 with tight CI), plus a structurally stronger cross-ancestry PRS-CSx construction with much larger variant count (1,271,239 vs 382,963), which is the more reliable differentiator given missing PRS-only metrics. Therefore PGS005313 is better-supported on the visible fields despite its lower full-model AUROC.

PGS001263 is the better-supported choice for the specific target trait atrial flutter because it has exact endpoint alignment across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (“Atrial flutter”) and it reports clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.617 and PGS-only R²=0.025), which can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling (well below h2_liability=0.144). In contrast, PGS002050 targets a broader combined phenotype (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”) rather than flutter alone and provides no PRS-only AUROC/R² (only partial correlation), making its predictive evidence less directly comparable for PRS quality despite higher variant count and larger training N. Both use only basic covariates and similar UKB-based development/evaluation, so the decisive advantages are PGS001263’s tighter phenotype fidelity and clearer PRS-only metrics.

PGS002755 is a closer match to the target trait as a general atopic eczema/atopic dermatitis endpoint (phenotyping_reported: incident atopic dermatitis), whereas PGS001773 targets a narrower subtype (moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis), which is a phenotype restriction relative to generic atopic eczema. Neither record provides PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R2 are missing for both); PGS001773’s very high AUROC=0.93 and R²=0.49 are full-model metrics with demographic/ethnicity covariates and are not comparable as standalone PRS evidence (and the R² is implausibly above the eczema heritability ceiling given in context). With metrics not cleanly comparable, structural signals favor PGS002755’s genome-wide PRS-CS model (~1.09M variants) over PGS001773’s 25-variant score, and PGS002755 also has much broader evaluation scale (n=337,910 EUR) than PGS001773 (n=676).

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all basal cell carcinoma), are EUR-only, use the same basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PC1-4), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so the full-model AUROC 0.64 in PGS000119 vs 0.632 in PGS000452 is not a clean PRS differentiator). PGS000452 has a slightly stronger evidence package on the visible record: it reports additional supporting metrics beyond AUROC (Nagelkerke R²=0.0487, Brier score, and a strong tail-risk OR top 1% vs rest=3.61), whereas PGS000119 provides only AUROC and per-SD OR. With otherwise near-identical design and similar per-SD OR (~1.65), the richer, more internally consistent performance reporting in PGS000452 makes it better-supported overall.

PGS001263 is the better match to the target trait (atrial flutter) with direct endpoint fidelity: trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are both specifically “Atrial flutter,” whereas PGS001339 is a combined phenotype (“Atrial fibrillation and flutter”) and explicitly time-to-event (TTE), which is a weaker match for a generic atrial flutter target. Both are from the same pan-trait UKB snpnet framework paper with identical training cohort/size, similar covariates (basic demographics/PCs), and the same validation sample size, so those factors don’t differentiate. On PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001263 is also slightly higher (PGS-only AUROC 0.617 vs 0.613; PGS-only R2 0.02517 vs 0.02447), and both are well below the heritability ceiling, so the small metric edge plus cleaner phenotype alignment favors PGS001263.

Both candidates have exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all basal cell carcinoma), EUR-only development/evaluation, and only basic covariates (age/sex/batch/PCs), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC 0.632 in PGS000454 vs 0.64 in PGS000119 is not a clean PRS-comparable differentiator). PGS000454 is better supported because it provides a richer performance package beyond AUROC, including Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0489), Brier score, and an extreme-tail OR (top 1% vs rest = 3.79), giving more direct evidence of risk stratification than PGS000119, which reports only AUROC and per-SD OR. Variant counts and per-SD OR are essentially similar (27 vs 32 variants; OR 1.661 vs 1.65), so the additional, more informative metrics in PGS000454 break the tie.

PGS000327 has clean endpoint fidelity: trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to autism spectrum disorder, whereas PGS002790 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported = "Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)") despite the ASD label. On performance evidence, neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², but PGS000327 provides supportive effect-size evidence (OR=1.33 per SD) and a higher reported R² (0.0245 vs partial R²=0.00546 for PGS002790), both well below the ASD heritability ceiling and thus plausible. Both candidates align well to the target depressive disorder (both map to EFO major depressive disorder; A is explicitly Major Depressive Disorder and B is Depression with the same EFO), and both are EUR-only GWAS/EVAL with similar genome-wide PRS-CS-style methods and ~1.09M variants. The key differentiator is performance evidence: PGS002759 reports a PRS effect size (OR per SD = 1.26, 95% CI 1.22–1.30), which is a directly PRS-comparable signal, whereas PGS003333 provides only a Nagelkerke pseudo-R2=0.022 that appears to be a full-model/unspecified covariate context (covariates listed as Unknown) and lacks PRS-only metrics or effect sizes. With cleaner disclosed basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/technical) and an interpretable PRS effect size, PGS002759 is better supported on the visible fields despite similar validation sample sizes.

PGS001783 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance and structural design for COPD: it reports a covariates-regressed-out/PGS-comparable Nagelkerke R2 of 0.0381, which is materially higher than PGS001332’s explicit PGS-only R2 of 0.00235 and is consistent with the trait’s liability h2 ceiling (~0.0388). Endpoint fidelity is essentially equivalent (both map to COPD; PGS001332’s phenotyping is a near-synonym composite “chronic obstructive airways disease/copd”). While PGS001332 has a larger validation sample and multi-ancestry evaluation, it comes from the known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“813 traits”) and shows weak PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC 0.5397; incremental AUROC 0.003 suggests the full-model AUROC is mostly covariate-driven). PGS001783 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far broader GWAS cohort sourcing and vastly more variants, and its PRS-only R2 evidence is stronger despite EUR-only evaluation and smaller validation n.

PGS003576 is better supported for the target “depressive disorder” because its endpoint is explicitly Major Depressive Disorder (lifetime) with phenotyping_reported = “Major depressive disorder,” matching the EFO mapping, and it shows broader external evaluation across multiple ancestries (AFR/AMR/ASN/EAS/EUR) rather than EUR-only. While neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R², PGS003576 at least provides an R² estimate (though it appears to be a generic/full-model R² and thus not ideal), whereas PGS002759 provides no R²/AUC metrics at all and only an OR=1.26 (moderate/weak). PGS002759 also comes from a cross-disease “family history and polygenic risk across 24 common diseases” framework-style paper with missing training details, making it less disease-focused and less well-characterized than PGS003576’s MDD-focused study context.

PGS004254 has cleaner endpoint fidelity to the target (phenotyping_reported and trait_reported are simply “Crohn’s disease”), whereas PGS001330 is explicitly a time-to-event (TTE) “Crohn’s disease [regional enteritis]”, which is a weaker match for generic Crohn’s disease risk per the provided guidance. On performance evidence, PGS001330 does report PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.5759; PGS-only R2 0.00621, below the h2_obs ceiling ~0.0122), but these indicate only modest PRS signal; PGS004254 lacks PGS-only AUC/R2 yet provides a strong per-SD effect size (OR 2.18) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach with far broader variant coverage (744,682 vs 220), which is structurally more appropriate than the sparse pan-trait UKB snpnet score (PGS001330 comes from the “813 traits” framework paper). Overall, the combination of better phenotype alignment and stronger structural/effect-size support favors PGS004254 despite missing PRS-only metrics.

PGS004862 is better supported for the target trait because it is the MTAG-enhanced dilated cardiomyopathy score (trait_reported: "Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG)") while keeping the same endpoint fidelity as PGS004861 (both have trait_efo and phenotyping_reported as dilated cardiomyopathy, same basic covariates, same EUR-only GWAS/EVAL, same validation n=347,585, same publication family). With no PGS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (only full-model metrics), the small full-model AUROC/R² differences are weak, but PGS004862 is slightly higher (AUROC 0.71 vs 0.70; R² 0.05 vs 0.048) and shows a stronger per-SD OR (1.76 vs 1.56). Domain guidance mildly prefers MTAG variants over base within the same disease family, so PGS004862 edges PGS004861.

PGS005170 is better supported for the target trait dementia because its phenotype alignment is direct (trait_reported: all-cause dementia; phenotyping_reported: incident all-cause dementia; trait_efo: dementia) and it is a large, integrative genome-wide PRS ensemble (24 component PRSs; 1,320,229 variants) with multi-ancestry evaluation reported (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR). Although it only reports a full-model AUROC (0.761) and an HR=1.25 and includes APOE genotype as a covariate (making the AUROC not PRS-comparable), it still provides a coherent dementia-focused risk score framework. In contrast, PGS000823 is primarily an Alzheimer’s disease score (trait_efo: Alzheimer disease) with only 23 genome-wide significant variants and no AUC/R2; it reports only a grouped HR (top vs bottom tertile 1.36) and has narrower evaluation (EUR only). Given the target is broad dementia, PGS005170’s endpoint match and stronger structural PRS construction outweigh PGS000823’s larger validation N.

Both candidates map to Alzheimer’s disease (trait_reported/trait_efo match) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on endpoint fidelity, covariate comparability, and structural signals. PGS002249 has closer endpoint alignment to the target trait dementia via phenotyping_reported="Incident dementia" (vs PGS000823 "Incident all-cause dementia" while labeled Alzheimer’s), and it uses a far more polygenic construction (LD clumping; 249,273 variants) than PGS000823’s 23 genome-wide significant hits, which is generally a stronger structural basis for a complex trait when PRS-only metrics are absent. Although PGS002249 includes heavier covariates (education, socioeconomic status, lifestyle categories) than PGS000823 (age, sex), the reported HR separation is also stronger (1.91 high vs low genetic risk vs 1.36 top vs bottom tertile), and the much larger validation sample (196,383 vs 12,978) provides additional—albeit weak—support. Net: PGS002249 is better supported overall; confidence is moderate because both lack clean PRS-only discrimination metrics and PGS002249’s covariates are less clean.

PGS000997 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.591 and PGS-only R2=0.0178 (with basic covariates listed), allowing a clean assessment of standalone PRS signal and a heritability-ceiling sanity check. PGS004544 has an endpoint-aligned ICD10 K57 phenotype and a large variant count, but it provides no AUROC/R2 at all (only an OR=1.32 with unknown covariates), making its predictive performance and comparability much less verifiable from the record. While PGS000997 comes from a pan-trait UKB framework and uses a time-to-event definition (both mild negatives), it still has clearer, directly comparable PRS-only metrics than PGS004544’s largely missing performance metadata.

Both candidates have good endpoint fidelity to diverticular disease (PGS004614: “Diverticular disease”; PGS004544: ICD10 K57 diverticular disease of intestine) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so performance is hard to compare. PGS004614 is favored because the only visible discrimination metric is an AUROC=0.76, but it is explicitly a full-model AUROC with covariates including family history (making it non-PRS-comparable); still, PGS004544 provides even less comparable performance evidence (no AUC/R2 at all, only an OR=1.32 per SD which is moderate). Additionally, PGS004614 shows broader evaluation ancestry (AFR/EUR/SAS) suggesting some transportability evidence beyond EUR-only evaluation in PGS004544. Given the heavy covariate concern for PGS004614 and sparse metric reporting for both, confidence remains low.

Both candidates target the same trait (Dilated cardiomyopathy (MTAG); EFO matches) and use the same method (PRS-CS) with broadly comparable, non-leaky covariates (A: age/sex/PCs; B: sex/PCs). The key differentiator is that PGS004951 reports PRS-comparable performance (explicit univariate PRS-only AUC=0.67 with CI and delta PRS/residual liability-scale R²=0.101), whereas PGS004862 only provides full-model AUROC=0.71 and R²=0.05 (not PRS-only and thus not comparable per policy). PGS004951 also has a higher per-SD OR (1.93 vs 1.76) and a substantially larger variant count (1,075,760 vs 709,534), supporting stronger PRS signal. Although PGS004862 has a much larger validation sample (347,585 vs 7,761), validation N is a weak tie-break and does not outweigh the cleaner PRS-only metric evidence in PGS004951.

PGS002304 has exact endpoint fidelity for the target (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported both “Follicular lymphoma”, trait_efo matches), whereas PGS000644 is labeled/phenotyped as “Nodular lymphoma” despite mapping to follicular lymphoma in trait_efo, creating a clearer phenotype-alignment concern. Neither record provides PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values are not cleanly comparable; still, PGS002304’s reported AUROC (0.61) is higher than PGS000644’s (0.538). PGS000644 has stronger structural properties (lassosum, ~2.2M variants) and reports additional metrics/effect sizes, but given the primary importance of endpoint fidelity and the lack of PRS-only metrics for either, the exact follicular-lymphoma phenotype match in PGS002304 outweighs PGS000644’s method/variant-count advantage.

PGS004951 is better supported for dilated cardiomyopathy because it provides explicit PRS-comparable performance evidence (Univariate/PRS-only AUC=0.67 with CI, plus delta PRS/residual liability-scale R²=0.101 and Nagelkerke delta=0.076), whereas PGS004861 reports only full-model AUROC=0.70 and full-model R²=0.048 (not clean PRS-only metrics). Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (both map to dilated cardiomyopathy; PGS004951’s “(MTAG)” and “Clinical dilated cardiomyopathy” remain aligned and MTAG is not penalized). Although PGS004861 has a much larger validation sample (n=347,585 vs n=7,761) and slightly cleaner/basic covariates, the lack of PRS-only metrics makes its apparent AUROC advantage non-comparable; PGS004951 also shows stronger effect size evidence (OR 1.93 vs 1.56) and higher variant count (1,075,760 vs 713,932) within the same method family (PRS-CS).

PGS001792 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.03209, which is directly interpretable as PRS signal and is below the glaucoma liability h2 ceiling (~0.0556), making it plausible. PGS000137 provides no PRS-only AUC/R2 (only a full-model AUROC=0.8), and its covariates include self-reported family history, which can inflate full-model discrimination and reduces comparability to standalone PRS performance. Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (both phenotyping_reported are POAG despite PGS000137’s broader trait_reported label), so the decision hinges on cleaner PRS-only metrics and covariate design, favoring PGS001792.

PGS004614 is the better-supported choice for the generic target “diverticular disease” because its endpoint is a direct disease diagnosis (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Diverticular disease”) and it comes from a disease-focused diverticular-disease GWAS paper, with multi-ancestry evaluation listed. Although it only reports a full-model AUROC (0.76) and lacks PRS-only metrics, its covariates include family history (making that AUROC non-PRS-comparable), so we cannot treat the 0.76 as strong PRS evidence—but structurally it is a genome-wide shrinkage score with very large variant coverage (1,082,282), which is a positive signal for a polygenic disease. In contrast, PGS000997 is explicitly a pan-trait UK Biobank framework score (“across 813 traits”) with a time-to-event phenotype and a very sparse model (5,757 variants); while it does provide clean PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.591, PGS R2 0.01777), those are modest and the framework+sparse/TTE packaging is a known generalization weakness versus a disease-focused genome-wide model. Overall, PGS004614’s disease-focused, endpoint-faithful, genome-wide construction outweighs PGS000997’s modest PRS-only metrics from a pan-trait sparse UKB framework.

Both candidates align well to the target (trait_efo Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported is a direct Dupuytren/palmar fascia contracture endpoint). PGS001254 is better-supported on PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.6646 and PGS-only R²=0.0247, whereas PGS002092 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0797) and has no PGS-only AUC/R² reported, making cross-model PRS discrimination harder to judge. PGS002092 has stronger structural/portability signals (LDpred2 genome-wide with 484k variants and multi-ancestry evaluation), but given the absence of standard PRS-only metrics on the record, the cleaner, directly comparable PRS-only AUROC/R² evidence in PGS001254 outweighs that advantage.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for dupuytren contracture (same trait_reported, trait_efo, phenotyping_reported), come from the same UKB portability paper, have the same training size (n=391,124), covariates, ancestry distribution, and validation sample size (n=18,971), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only partial-r). With performance nearly tied (partial-r 0.0797 for PGS002092 vs 0.0783 for PGS001880, overlapping CIs), the main differentiator is structural: PGS002092 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (484,484 vs 2,443), which is generally favored for polygenic traits when other evidence is equal. Hence PGS002092 is slightly better-supported, but confidence is only moderate because the empirical metric difference is minimal.

Both candidates are endpoint-aligned to gout (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match). PGS001789 provides an explicit PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.0312), whereas PGS004047 reports only full-model metrics (AUROC and R²) with no PGS-only AUC/R², making its performance less comparable for PRS quality ranking. PGS001789 is also developed across many biobanks with multi-ancestry GWAS and tri-ancestry evaluation, supporting broader transportability than PGS004047’s UKB-only EUR development and EUR/SAS evaluation. Although PGS004047 includes strong effect sizes (OR~2 per SD), the lack of PRS-only performance metrics and narrower development context make it less well-supported overall than PGS001789.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target follicular lymphoma: same trait_efo (follicular lymphoma), same reported/phenotyping label (“Nodular lymphoma”), same publication/date, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC differences are weak tie-breakers; however PGS000644 has slightly higher AUROC (0.538 vs 0.532) and slightly higher pseudo-R² (0.00349 vs 0.00282) and per-SD OR (1.149 vs 1.133). PGS000643 has a higher top-1% vs rest OR (2.49 vs 1.48), but given the otherwise identical setup and overlapping uncertainty, the small overall discrimination/effect-size edge favors PGS000644. Confidence is low because the metrics are full-model and differences are marginal.

Both candidates align well to the target (same trait_efo Dupuytren Contracture; phenotyping_reported is a direct Dupuytren/Dupuytren’s disease endpoint for both). PGS001254 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.6646 and PGS-only R²=0.0247, whereas PGS001880 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0783) and has no PRS-only AUC/R², making cross-model comparison weaker. Covariates are similarly basic in both (age/sex/PCs/array-type style), so no major leakage advantage. PGS001880 has broader evaluation ancestries and many more variants (2443 vs 11), but without PRS-comparable metrics this doesn’t outweigh PGS001254’s clearer standalone PRS performance evidence. Confidence is moderate because PGS001880’s multi-ancestry evaluation could indicate better portability, but the lack of comparable AUC/R² limits support.

PGS004944 is better supported for the target glaucoma because its endpoint is explicitly primary open-angle glaucoma with coherent mapping (trait_reported POAG; trait_efo open-angle glaucoma) and it shows cleaner covariate handling (age/age^2/sex/ancestry only) plus a strong PRS effect size (OR 1.74 per SD). It also has much broader evaluation context (selected validation ancestries spanning African unspecified, Hispanic/LatAm, East Asian, South Asian, European) and a very large validation sample (n=407,667), supporting transportability. In contrast, PGS000137 has a broader trait label (Glaucoma) but phenotyping is still POAG, and its reported AUROC=0.8 is only a full-model metric with explicit inclusion of self-reported family history (a leakage/packaging concern), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 or effect size to isolate the PRS contribution. With both lacking PRS-only metrics, the stronger effect-size evidence and cleaner covariates favor PGS004944.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target (same trait_efo Hashimoto’s thyroiditis; same phenotyping_reported/trait_reported lymphocytic thyroiditis; same method PRSCS; same evaluation ancestry mix and identical validation n=94,651) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is discounted). With endpoints and covariates equally uninformative (covariates unknown for both), the best differentiators are effect-size strength and any structural/study-support differences: PGS005271 shows stronger per-SD association (OR 1.55 vs 1.42; β 0.44 vs 0.35) and slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.630 vs 0.605), plus a marginally larger variant count and broader listed development cohorts. These consistent (though modest) advantages make PGS005271 better supported overall.

Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all = gout). However, PGS001789 provides an explicitly PRS-comparable metric (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.0312), which is interpretable as PRS signal and is below the gout heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0525), whereas PGS004160 reports only full-model AUROC/R² (and no PGS-only AUC/R²), making its performance less comparable for PRS ranking. PGS001789 is also developed across many biobanks with multi-ancestry GWAS inputs and broad evaluation, supporting transportability, while PGS004160 is UKB-only development (EUR) with smaller stated training n=6,704 and limited evaluation ancestries. Despite PGS004160 showing effect sizes, the lack of PRS-only metrics and narrower development context makes it less well-supported than PGS001789 on the visible fields.

Both candidates are endpoint-faithful to Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (trait_efo matches; phenotyping_reported is the same “lymphocytic thyroiditis”), come from the same publication family, have the same evaluation ancestry mix (MAE 100%) and the same validation sample size (n=94,651), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). With phenotype and transportability essentially tied, the differentiators are structural/effect-size signals: PGS005272 uses PRSCS with genome-wide coverage (1,085,142 variants) and shows a much stronger per-SD effect size (OR≈1.42) than PGS005270 (OR≈1.04) despite PGS005270 having a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.639 vs 0.605), a difference that is small and not reliable for ranking without covariate details. Therefore PGS005272 is better-supported as a standalone PRS.

Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_efo Hashimoto’s thyroiditis; phenotyping_reported lymphocytic thyroiditis), come from the same publication family, and have identical evaluation ancestry mix and validation sample size (n=94,651), so endpoint fidelity and transportability do not differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2; the only AUROC shown is a full-model AUROC (0.6297 for PGS005271 vs 0.6387 for PGS005270), which is not a reliable PRS-comparable discriminator, especially with covariates listed as Unknown for both. The strongest differentiators are structural and effect-size evidence: PGS005271 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRSCS) with ~1,085,156 variants and shows a much stronger per-SD effect (OR≈1.55) consistent with meaningful PRS signal, whereas PGS005270 is a very sparse P+T score (55 variants) with a near-null reported OR≈1.04. Given the lack of PRS-only metrics, the combination of stronger method/coverage and materially stronger effect size makes PGS005271 better supported despite the slightly higher full-model AUROC for PGS005270.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all = gout), come from the same publication, have the same training cohort (UKB), training N (6,704), covariates=0, and the same evaluation ancestry mix and validation N (90,274), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model AUROC/R²), so the decision rests on the limited comparative signals available. PGS004160 shows consistently better reported performance in the selected European validation record than PGS004047 (higher full-model AUROC 0.6936 vs 0.6851; higher R² 0.0893 vs 0.0801; slightly higher OR per SD 2.05 vs 2.00), and it is an ensemble/multi-PRS method (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) which is a positive structural signal over a single-score LDpred2.CV when other fields are matched. Given the lack of PRS-only metrics, confidence is moderate rather than high.

Both candidates align well to the target (glaucoma) and specifically primary open-angle glaucoma, but PGS001792 has cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports a PGS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 of 0.03209, which is interpretable as PRS signal and is below the provided liability h2 ceiling (~0.0556). In contrast, PGS004944 provides no PGS-only AUC/R2 and only a full-model AUROC (0.748), which the guidance says is not a valid substitute for PRS performance. While PGS004944 reports a strong per-SD OR (1.74) and broader listed validation ancestries, the lack of PRS-comparable metrics makes its support less directly comparable than PGS001792’s explicit PRS-only R2; both use only basic demographic/ancestry covariates without obvious clinical leakage.

PGS002304 has exact endpoint fidelity to the target across all visible fields (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Follicular lymphoma”), whereas PGS000643 is internally inconsistent on the surface label (trait_reported and phenotyping_reported “Nodular lymphoma” despite trait_efo mapping to follicular lymphoma), creating ambiguity about the actual evaluated endpoint. Neither record reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values (0.61 for PGS002304 vs 0.532 for PGS000643) are not cleanly comparable PRS metrics; however, PGS000643’s additional metrics (Nagelkerke R²=0.00282, OR per SD=1.133) suggest weak PRS signal, while PGS002304 provides no PRS-isolated metrics at all. PGS000643 is structurally stronger (PRS-CS, ~1.0M variants, explicit basic covariates) and has larger validation (n=3,256 vs n=197), but given the endpoint-label ambiguity and weak reported PRS signal, the exact phenotype match of PGS002304 narrowly wins on the primary criterion (endpoint fidelity), with low confidence due to missing PRS-only metrics and PGS002304’s small validation and unknown covariates.

Both candidates align on the target concept (trait_reported/trait_efo = heart failure), but PGS001790 provides a PRS-comparable performance metric (PGS-only / covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 = 0.006981), whereas PGS005097 reports only full-model AUROC (0.72) with no PGS-only AUC/R2, making its discrimination evidence largely non-comparable for PRS ranking. PGS001790’s reported PRS R2 is also well below the heart-failure heritability ceiling noted in the context, supporting metric sanity. Although PGS005097 has a more diverse evaluation ancestry and a disease-focused publication, the lack of PRS-only metrics versus PGS001790’s explicit PRS R2 is the decisive evidence advantage here.

PGS002763 has the cleaner endpoint match to the target trait: phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Hip osteoarthritis,” whereas PGS002728 uses “Total hip replacement,” a treatment/proxy endpoint that can reflect access/clinical decision factors beyond disease status. Neither candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so PGS002728’s reported AUROC=0.66 is a full-model metric (age, sex) and is not a comparable PRS metric; in contrast PGS002763 provides a PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.38, moderate signal) that is directly informative about PRS discrimination. Structurally, PGS002763 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.05M variants versus PGS002728’s 44 genome-wide significant SNPs, which is generally favorable for a polygenic trait like hip OA. Both are EUR-only evaluation, so ancestry doesn’t differentiate.

PGS001790 is the better-supported choice for the target trait heart failure because it has a direct endpoint match (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Heart failure”) and, crucially, reports a PRS-comparable metric: a covariates-regressed-out/PGS-only Nagelkerke R2=0.006981, which is interpretable and below the heart-failure heritability ceiling noted in the context. In contrast, PGS005077 targets a narrower/administrative phecode endpoint (“Congestive heart failure (CHF), NOS (PheCode 428.1)”) and provides no PGS-only AUC/R2; its visible discrimination is a full-model C-index (~0.754) which is not comparable as a PRS metric. Although PGS005077 reports an OR=1.452 (moderate) and has multi-ancestry evaluation, the lack of PRS-only performance metrics makes it less cleanly supported than PGS001790’s explicit PRS-only R2 evidence.

PGS001320 is better-supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.629 and PGS-only R2=0.0649 (no covariates), enabling a clean PRS-vs-PRS comparison and a heritability-ceiling sanity check. PGS004236 reports only a full-model AUROC=0.764 (no PGS-only AUC/R2), and its covariates include BMI and smoking plus race/ethnic background and site, making the AUROC more likely covariate-inflated and not comparable as standalone PRS evidence. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (hypertension), though PGS004236’s phenotyping is explicitly prevalent hypertension while PGS001320 is generic hypertension. Despite PGS004236 being disease-focused and multi-cohort with a strong OR=2.1, the lack of PRS-only metrics and heavier covariate set make its support weaker than PGS001320’s clean PRS-only reporting.

Both candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match Hodgkin’s disease / Hodgkins lymphoma), come from the same publication, use the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and have identical EUR-only training/evaluation context and validation size (n=775), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Given that, PGS000639 is better supported by consistently stronger reported performance/effect evidence in the selected validation record: higher AUROC (0.62 vs 0.601), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0276 vs 0.0193), higher OR per SD (1.476 vs 1.377), and higher top-1% vs rest OR (2.64 vs 1.62). PGS000638 lacks any compensating advantage beyond being a similar small-variant GWAS-hits score.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target hyperthyroidism via the clinically dominant subtype Graves’ disease (same trait_reported/efo/phenotyping_reported, same method PRSCS, same evaluation ancestry mix and identical validation sample size n=94,651, and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 with covariates unknown). With no PRS-comparable metrics, the only differentiators are small full-model AUROC/effect-size differences and minor structural differences: PGS005265 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.6652 vs 0.6637), stronger OR per SD (1.625 vs 1.543) and beta (0.486 vs 0.434), and trivially more variants (1,085,173 vs 1,085,170). These are modest, so confidence is low, but they consistently favor PGS005265.

Both candidates match the target concept well (trait_reported/trait_efo are identical), but PGS002763 has cleaner endpoint fidelity for generic “hip osteoarthritis” (phenotyping_reported: Hip osteoarthritis) whereas PGS004882 is explicitly incident/time-to-event (phenotyping_reported: Incident hip osteoarthritis), which is a mild mismatch for a generic disease-risk target. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we rely on effect sizes and design signals: both show similar moderate per-SD effects (PGS002763 OR=1.38 vs PGS004882 HR=1.4), and PGS004882’s reported C-index=0.6 is a full-model metric (not PRS-only) and thus not a strong differentiator. PGS002763 also uses only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, technical), while PGS004882’s framework-style incidence modeling plus minimal covariates doesn’t provide clearer PRS-isolated performance. Overall, PGS002763 is the better-supported, more directly aligned disease PRS for the target.

Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo = Hypertension; phenotyping_reported = prevalent hypertension) and use the same covariate set, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only very similar full-model AUROC: 0.764 vs 0.763, which is not a reliable differentiator). PGS004236 is better supported because it provides additional PRS-relevant evidence via an effect size (OR=2.1 per SD, strong signal), whereas PGS004234 reports no effect sizes. Candidate B (PGS000196) shows a higher full-model AUROC (0.79 vs 0.65) but it is evaluated on a very small validation sample (n=245) and its phenotyping_reported is more context-restricted ("diagnosis in patient with arthritis"), suggesting a narrower outpatient/triage setting rather than a general SLE endpoint. Candidate A (PGS000754) has cleaner endpoint wording (straight SLE diagnosis), much broader validation support (n=7,733) and a structurally stronger genome-wide shrinkage approach with far more variants (lassosum; 293,684 vs P+T; 55), which is a more reliable differentiator when PRS-only metrics are absent. Therefore PGS000754 is better supported overall despite the lower full-model AUROC.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia; phenotyping_reported=Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia) and use similarly clean basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported in either record (so full-model AUROC/C-index are not decisive PRS-comparable metrics).
