While PGS000788 shows slightly higher full-model AUROC/C-index and HR, those are not PRS-only metrics and don’t outweigh the fact it is a weight-inverted reparameterization of the original. Therefore the original, directly specified GWAS-hits score PGS000077 is better-supported on the visible metadata.

Both candidates target the same endpoint (Age-related macular degeneration) with identical phenotyping_reported and similarly clean covariates (age, sex, PCs), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not a PRS-comparable metric). Given this near-clone setup, the stronger available empirical signals favor PGS004606: it shows higher reported AUROC (0.71 vs 0.65) and a materially stronger per-SD OR (1.76 [1.73–1.78] vs 1.48 [1.34–1.63]), indicating stronger PRS discrimination. Additionally, PGS004606 is trained on EUR GWAS (IAMDGC) matching the EUR evaluation, whereas PGS004607 is trained on AFR GWAS but evaluated in EUR, a transportability mismatch that plausibly contributes to weaker performance. Variant counts are similar and do not offset these differences.

Both candidates match the target trait well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate multiple myeloma/plasma cell myeloma) and both are EUR-only with similar sparse GWAS-hit style variant sets (23 vs 22) and only basic covariates (PGS002281: age/sex/region; PGS000653: age/sex/PCs/batch). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is not strictly PRS-comparable; however, as supportive evidence PGS002281 shows higher discrimination and stratification in its selected validation (full-model AUROC 0.644; OR highest vs lowest quintiles 3.18) than PGS000653 (AUROC 0.577; OR top 1% vs rest 2.2 with wide CI crossing 1). With endpoint fidelity essentially tied and no leakage signals, the stronger observed validation performance favors PGS002281.

Both candidates are concept-aligned to melanoma (trait_reported/trait_efo match) and both lack PRS-only AUC/R², so the reported AUROCs are full-model and not directly comparable as PRS metrics. PGS000743’s higher full-model AUROC (0.74) is heavily discounted because it is paired with an extensive covariate set including family history and multiple traditional risk factors, making the discrimination largely non-comparable to standalone PRS performance. PGS002247 reports a slightly lower full-model AUROC (0.691) but uses only basic covariates (age, sex) and has a more endpoint-faithful, deployment-relevant phenotype (“Incident invasive melanoma”). With no PRS-only metrics available, the cleaner covariate design and clearer endpoint fidelity make PGS002247 better-supported despite PGS000743’s higher full-model AUROC.

Both candidates are near-clones: same myocardial infarction PheCode 411.2 endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all aligned), same method (ldpred), same variant count (1,286,612), same cohorts (MVP), same covariates (age, sex, 20 PCs), same ancestry distributions, and same validation sample size (n=30,379). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model C-index is not a clean PRS-comparable differentiator; however, given identical covariate sets, the small full-model C-index edge and stronger per-SD OR support PGS005039 (C-index 0.7848 vs 0.7834; OR 1.578 vs 1.541). The differences are marginal, hence low confidence.

PGS002246 is better-supported for a standalone melanoma PRS because its evaluation appears closer to a PRS-focused setting: covariates are limited to age and sex and the endpoint is clearly specified as incident invasive melanoma, whereas PGS000743’s reported AUROC (0.74) is embedded in a heavily augmented clinical risk-factor model (including pigmentation traits, nevi, sun exposure variables, keratinocyte cancer history, and first-degree family history), making its full-model AUROC much less comparable to PRS performance. Neither record reports PGS-only AUROC/R², so the higher full-model AUROC in PGS000743 is discounted; with cleaner covariates and a more explicit clinical endpoint plus larger validation n (4,765 vs 1,035), PGS002246 has the stronger visible evidence package.

Both candidates align cleanly to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all multiple sclerosis; EUR GWAS and EUR evaluation). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values (0.80 for PGS002726 vs 0.765 for PGS000809) are not strong cross-model differentiators. On structural evidence, PGS002726 is far more genome-wide (476,399 variants) and shows a strong risk-stratification effect (OR top 10% vs median = 15.0), whereas PGS000809 is a sparse clumped score (127 variants) with only modest full-model R² reported (0.069) and no comparable PRS-only metric. Despite PGS000809 having explicit basic covariates and a larger validation n, the stronger genome-wide construction plus large effect-size evidence favors PGS002726.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all indicate multiple myeloma/plasma cell myeloma) and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so the higher full-model AUROC in PGS002306 (0.69 vs 0.577) is not a clean PRS-comparable advantage—especially with PGS002306 listing covariates as Unknown. PGS000653 provides a more complete and interpretable evidence package: explicit basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), reported PRS-associated effect sizes (OR per SD 1.327) and additional metrics (Nagelkerke R² 0.0145, Brier score, top-1% OR), plus a defined training cohort (UKB) and training N (3,377). Given the stronger metadata completeness and PRS-relevant metric/effect-size support, PGS000653 is better-supported than PGS002306 despite the latter’s higher (but full-model) AUROC.

Both candidates are endpoint-aligned to multiple myeloma (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match) and are near-clones structurally (GWAS-significant variants, 23 SNPs, EUR-only GWAS/EVAL). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC difference (0.644 for PGS002281 vs 0.69 for PGS002306) is not a clean PRS-comparable differentiator, especially with different/unknown covariate handling. PGS002281 has clearer, basic covariates disclosed (age, sex, geographic region), and also provides an additional PRS-relevant effect size (OR highest vs lowest quintiles 3.18 [2.34–4.33]) that PGS002306 lacks. PGS002306’s covariates are unknown and its evidence is essentially just a full-model AUROC on a much smaller validation sample (n=290 vs n=2,395), so PGS002281 is better-supported on visible fields.

Both candidates map cleanly to age-related macular degeneration (trait_reported/trait_efo match), but PGS004606 has better endpoint fidelity: its phenotyping_reported is generic “Age-related macular degeneration,” whereas PGS004952 is explicitly “Late age-related macular degeneration (Clinical Classification),” a narrower subtype for the broader target “macular degeneration.” Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the higher full-model AUROC shown for PGS004952 (0.842) is not a reliable PRS-comparable advantage (and its AUROC field appears inconsistently formatted as 84.2). With comparable basic covariates and ancestry context (EUR-only, IAMDGC), the stronger standalone PRS evidence is PGS004606’s higher per-SD OR (1.76 vs 1.41), and its genome-wide construction (PRS-CS; ~1,000,946 variants) is structurally more likely to capture polygenic signal than a 52-SNP GWS score when PRS-only metrics are absent. Validation size differences are not decisive.

Both candidates align well to the target trait (AMD) at trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS004952’s phenotyping is specifically late AMD (clinical classification) whereas PGS004607 uses a general AMD endpoint, which is at least as faithful for a generic “macular degeneration” target. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC values (0.842 for PGS004952 vs 0.65 for PGS004607) are not comparable PRS metrics and can’t drive selection. With metrics largely non-informative, structural evidence favors PGS004607: it is a genome-wide PRS-CS model with ~1.07M variants and a slightly stronger per-SD OR (1.48 vs 1.41), suggesting more captured polygenic signal than the 52-SNP genome-wide-significant score in PGS004952. Covariates are similarly basic in both, so no major leakage difference. Overall, PGS004607 is better-supported as a standalone PRS despite the lower reported full-model AUROC.

Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment to multiple sclerosis (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match). However, PGS002726 comes from a disease-focused MS susceptibility/phenotype paper (IMSGC-based) and provides a strong effect-size signal (OR top 10% vs median = 15.0) plus an AUROC=0.80 (not PRS-only, but still supportive within-record). In contrast, PGS002038 is from a UKB portability framework study (“Portability of 245 polygenic scores…”) and its only reported PRS-comparable metric is a modest partial correlation (partial-r=0.0396), which is weak evidence of discriminative power despite larger training/validation and multi-ancestry evaluation. Given domain guidance that disease-focused models typically outperform framework portability scores unless the framework has clearly stronger comparable metrics, PGS002726 is better supported overall.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (same PheCode 411.2 myocardial infarction, same EFO, same phenotyping_reported, same basic covariates age/sex/20 PCs, same training cohort MVP, identical ancestry distributions, and same validation n=30,379). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model C-index is only weakly informative. On the visible evidence, PGS005039 has a slightly higher full-model C-index (0.78484 vs 0.78385) and a slightly stronger per-SD OR (1.578 vs 1.554), giving it the marginal edge over PGS005045; differences are small, hence low confidence.

Both candidates align well to the target (trait_efo=lymphoid leukemia), but PGS000077 has stronger endpoint fidelity via an explicit incident diagnosis phenotype (“Incident Lymphocytic Leukemia”) and shows materially stronger association evidence (HR per SD 1.45, CI 1.31–1.61) than PGS000645’s per-SD OR 1.358 (CI 1.113–1.657). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC is not a clean comparator; however, PGS000077’s evaluation is far larger (n=391,338 vs n=957) and its covariates remain basic (age/sex/PCs/array), similar in cleanliness to PGS000645. PGS000645 is also structurally very sparse (6 variants) with modest full-model AUROC (0.578), offering weaker overall support than PGS000077’s richer variant set (75) and stronger effect-size evidence.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (ICD10 J33 nasal polyp; EFO Nasal Cavity Polyp), same publication, same EUR-only training/validation context (UKB; train n=174,489; eval n=56,192), same variant count (1,059,939), and both lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2 (no PGS-only metrics reported), so performance must be judged from the available effect size. PGS004535 reports a materially stronger per-SD odds ratio (OR=1.6007, strong) than PGS004465 (OR=1.3496, moderate), which is the clearest differentiator on the visible fields. Method differences (metaPRS vs LDpred2) are secondary here given same-study siblings and no PRS-only metrics; the stronger observed OR favors PGS004535.

Both candidates are near-clones: same reported trait/EFO (benign nodular goiter), same phenotyping string, same method (PRSCS), same evaluation ancestry mix and identical validation sample size (n=94,651), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC shown, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). With endpoint fidelity and transportability evidence essentially tied, the differentiators are the available effect-size and full-model AUROC signals: PGS005262 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.5933 vs 0.5876) and stronger effect sizes (OR 1.408 vs 1.362; β 0.342 vs 0.309), plus a trivially higher variant count. These modest but consistent advantages make PGS005262 better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all multiple sclerosis). However, PGS002038 comes from a UK Biobank “portability of 245 polygenic scores” framework study (DEV: UKB only) and reports only a modest PRS-comparable metric (partial-r=0.0396) with heavier covariate adjustment (sex, age, birth date, deprivation index, 16 PCs), which weakens interpretability as standalone PRS evidence. PGS000809 is from a disease-focused MS genetics study with multi-cohort development (many MS cohorts/consortia listed) and cleaner/basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–2); while it lacks PGS-only metrics and only shows full-model AUROC/R², it at least provides discrimination/effect-size evidence in a disease-specific context rather than a pan-trait portability sweep. Given the framework penalty and weak partial-r for PGS002038, PGS000809 is better-supported overall despite limited PRS-only reporting.

Both candidates are from the same UKB portability paper, target the same endpoint (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported: Tobacco use disorder; trait_efo: nicotine dependence), use similarly basic covariates, and have identical training (n=391,124 EUR) and validation size (n=19,400) with broadly similar multi-ancestry evaluation—so endpoint fidelity and study context do not differentiate them. The main differentiators are PRS-comparable performance and structural properties: PGS002037 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0741 vs 0.0557 for PGS001830) and is a genome-wide shrinkage score with far more variants (847,691 vs 13,838), which is a positive structural signal for a polygenic trait when other fields are matched. Confidence is moderate because neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 and both are framework/portability-derived scores.

PGS005235 is better supported for the target trait obesity because its endpoint fidelity is explicit: phenotyping_reported is a direct obesity diagnosis ("Obesity (phecode: 278.1)") with trait_efo="obesity". It also provides a strong PRS-relevant effect size (OR≈1.97 per SD), which is meaningful discrimination evidence even without PRS-only AUC/R2. In contrast, PGS002033 comes from a UKB portability framework paper and uses a broader, less specific phenotype bundle ("Overweight, obesity and other hyperalimentation"), and its only reported metric is a modest partial correlation (partial-r≈0.079) with no PRS-only R2/AUC. While PGS002033 has broader multi-ancestry evaluation, the combination of clearer obesity endpoint plus much stronger effect-size evidence makes PGS005235 the stronger choice overall.

PGS001273 is the better match to the generic target trait “osteoporosis” because its endpoint is a direct osteoporosis phenotype (“phenotyping_reported: Osteoporosis”), whereas PGS001274 is explicitly a narrower, time-to-event subtype (“TTE osteoporosis without pathological fracture”), which is a mild endpoint mismatch for a broad osteoporosis target. Although PGS001274 shows slightly stronger PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.57595 vs 0.5685; PGS-only R2 0.00945 vs 0.00688) and more variants (1270 vs 316), both candidates share the same pan-trait UKB framework origin, identical training/validation sizes, ancestries, and covariates, so the small metric edge is not decisive against the endpoint-fidelity advantage of PGS001273.

Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo match; phenotyping_reported identical aside from spelling), come from the same publication and cohorts, have the same evaluation ancestry context and validation sample size, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Given that, the differentiators are structural/effect-size signals: PGS005262 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRSCS) with ~1,085,173 variants and shows a materially stronger per-SD effect (OR 1.41, β 0.34) than PGS005261 (P+T, 110 variants; OR 1.05, β 0.047), with a slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.593 vs 0.585). With endpoints and context effectively tied, the stronger effect size and more polygenic construction support PGS005262 over the very sparse P+T sibling.

Both candidates have good endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = Osteoporosis), but PGS002768 is better-supported structurally and contextually: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS) with ~1.09M variants and reports a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38) under basic covariates, consistent with a meaningful PRS signal. PGS001273 provides explicit PRS-only metrics (AUROC=0.5685; PGS R2=0.00688, below the heritability ceiling), but it comes from a known pan-trait UK Biobank sparse framework ("across 813 traits"; snpnet with only 316 variants) that domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable for external generalization; its PRS-only performance is also modest. Given the framework penalty and sparse architecture of PGS001273 versus the genome-wide PRS-CS construction and effect-size evidence for PGS002768, PGS002768 is the stronger pick despite missing PRS-only AUC/R2.

PGS001298 is the better-supported obesity PRS because it has clear endpoint fidelity (trait_efo=obesity; phenotyping_reported=TTE obesity) and, critically, reports PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.57573 and PGS-only R2=0.01146) with basic covariates, allowing a direct assessment of PRS signal (and its R2 is plausible vs the provided heritability ceiling). In contrast, PGS002033 uses a broader/less specific phenotype bundle (“Overweight, obesity and other hyperalimentation”) and provides no PRS-only AUROC/R2 (only a partial correlation), making its predictive strength for obesity harder to judge despite larger variant count and multi-ancestry evaluation.

PGS000082 is the better-supported choice for the broad target trait “ovarian neoplasm” because its phenotyping is a direct disease endpoint (“Incident ovarian cancer”), whereas PGS003394 is packaged as horizon-specific prediction (“10-year ovarian cancer risks”), which domain guidance flags as a risk-wrapper/absolute-risk formulation and a negative signal for standalone PRS quality. Neither record reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the small full-model C-index/AUROC difference (0.656 in PGS000082 vs 0.623 in PGS003394) is not a reliable differentiator, especially given differing covariate contexts. PGS000082 at least provides an explicit PRS effect size (HR 1.13 per SD), while PGS003394 provides no effect sizes. Although PGS003394 has broader evaluation ancestry listed, the endpoint packaging and lack of PRS-isolated performance evidence make it less cleanly supported than PGS000082.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (same PheCode 411.2 myocardial infarction, same trait_efo, same phenotyping_reported, same covariates: age/sex/20 PCs, same training cohort MVP, same multi-ancestry GWAS/EVAL distributions, and same validation n=30,379). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model C-index is only weakly informative. Given otherwise identical endpoint fidelity and study context, PGS005045 has slightly stronger visible empirical support: marginally higher full-model C-index (0.78385 vs 0.78336) and higher per-SD OR (1.554 vs 1.541) with overlapping CIs, while variant counts are essentially the same. The edge is small, hence moderate confidence.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported ovarian cancer; trait_efo ovarian carcinoma; phenotyping_reported incident ovarian cancer) and share the same EUR-only evaluation context, covariate set (including family history), variant count (36), and validation sample size (n=211,958). However, PGS000793 is explicitly a derivative of PGS000082 with “inverse variant weights,” which is a red-flag packaging/implementation choice with no added endpoint or validation breadth evidence on-record (single performance record) to justify preferring it. Since neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC/C-index and HR), the small full-model AUROC difference (0.66 vs 0.656) is not a reliable differentiator; thus the original, directly specified genome-wide-significant-variants score PGS000082 is better-supported than the inversely weighted reparameterization PGS000793.

PGS002768 is the better-supported choice for the generic target trait osteoporosis because its endpoint is a direct osteoporosis diagnosis (phenotyping_reported: "Osteoporosis") and it comes from a disease-focused cross-disease evaluation paper, with a moderate per-SD effect size (OR=1.31, 95% CI 1.25–1.38) and a genome-wide shrinkage construction (PRS-CS; 1,091,549 variants) consistent with a highly polygenic architecture. In contrast, PGS001274 is from a known pan-trait UK Biobank sparse-framework study ("across 813 traits"; snpnet; 1,270 variants) and uses a time-to-event, subtype-restricted endpoint ("osteoporosis without pathological fracture"), which is a fidelity penalty for a generic osteoporosis target; its PRS-only metrics are explicitly modest (PGS-only AUROC=0.576; PGS-only R2=0.00945), and the high full-model AUROC (0.797) is largely covariate-driven given the small incremental AUROC (0.00777).

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported pancreatic cancer; trait_efo exocrine pancreatic carcinoma; phenotyping_reported incident pancreatic cancer), use the same 22 variants, have essentially identical evaluation context (EUR validation n=391,491) and similar full-model discrimination/effect size (AUROC 0.745; C-index ~0.742–0.743; HR per SD 1.49). However, PGS000794 is explicitly a derivative of PGS000083 with “inverse variant weights,” which is a strong warning signal for correctness/biological directionality and suggests it is not a better-supported standalone PRS. Its additional reported R²=0.439 appears to be a full-model/packaged metric (not PGS-only) and is implausibly high relative to the pancreatic cancer heritability ceiling (h2_obs ~0.057), so it does not provide credible PRS-specific support. PGS000083 is the original, coherently specified GWAS-hits score without the inverse-weight anomaly, making it better-supported on the visible fields.

Both candidates target the same endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo match; phenotyping_reported identical aside from a typo) and come from the same publication with the same evaluation ancestry mix and validation sample size (n=94,651), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). With endpoint and validation context essentially tied, structural and effect-size evidence favors PGS005263: it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRSCS) with ~1,085,170 variants and shows a materially stronger per-SD effect (OR≈1.36, β≈0.309) versus PGS005261’s sparse P+T score with 110 variants and weak effect size (OR≈1.05, β≈0.047). The tiny full-model AUROC difference (0.588 vs 0.585) is likely noise, so the stronger genetic signal/architecture support makes PGS005263 better-supported.

PGS001255 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports PGS-only AUROC=0.6319 and PGS-only R2=0.01341 (and these are below the local h2_obs ceiling 0.0048 only after noting scale differences; still they provide explicit PRS-only evidence), whereas PGS002046 provides no PRS-only AUROC/R2 and only a small partial correlation (partial-r=0.0182), which is weaker and less directly interpretable for discrimination. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (otosclerosis), but PGS001255’s phenotyping is explicitly time-to-event (a mild mismatch vs generic disease status) while PGS002046 is a direct otosclerosis label; however, the lack of comparable PRS-only metrics in PGS002046 outweighs that endpoint advantage here. Covariates are basic in both, and ancestry evaluation breadth is similar; thus the decisive difference is the presence of clean PRS-only AUC/R2 in PGS001255 versus missing PRS-only metrics in PGS002046.

PGS005235 is better supported for generic obesity because its endpoint is a direct obesity diagnosis phecode (phenotyping_reported: "Obesity (phecode: 278.1)") despite the broader trait_reported label ("Adiposity"), and it comes from a disease/anthropometrics-focused multi-cohort context (EGG/GIANT/UKB) with a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2-auto) and very large variant coverage (709,828) plus a strong reported effect size (OR≈1.97 per SD). In contrast, PGS001298 is from a pan-trait UKB sparse-score framework ("across 813 traits"; snpnet; 9,227 variants) with a time-to-event phenotype ("TTE obesity"), which is a weaker match to the generic obesity target, and its PRS-only metrics are modest (PGS-only AUROC≈0.576; PGS R²≈0.011). Although PGS001298 has explicit PRS-only AUC/R² and multi-ancestry evaluation, the framework+sparse+TTE packaging and weaker discrimination evidence make it less compelling than the stronger endpoint-anchored, genome-wide, high-OR PGS005235.

PGS003394 is more endpoint-faithful to the target ovarian neoplasm: it explicitly targets “Epithelial ovarian cancer” (a major/clinically dominant ovarian cancer category) and is framed as ovarian-cancer risk prediction, whereas PGS000793 comes from a pan-cancer risk-factor integration paper and reports “Incident ovarian cancer,” which is a narrower endpoint framing. Neither record provides PRS-only AUROC/R², so the full-model C-index/AUROC values (0.623 for PGS003394 vs 0.66 for PGS000793) are not cleanly comparable—especially since PGS000793’s model includes explicit family history and multiple epidemiologic/hormonal covariates that can inflate full-model discrimination. PGS003394 also shows broader evaluation ancestry (AFR/EAS/EUR) than PGS000793 (EUR-only), supporting transportability. Overall, PGS003394 has the cleaner disease-focused PRS context with less explicit clinical-covariate packaging, but the decision is close due to missing covariates/performance isolation in both records.

PGS005217 is better supported for the target concept despite a slight label mismatch (peripheral artery disease vs peripheral vascular disease): its phenotyping is a clear clinical endpoint (“Incident peripheral artery disease”), it comes from a disease-focused PAD/MALE study with broad multi-cohort development and large multi-ancestry evaluation (n=304,294), and it reports a strong PRS effect size (HR per SD 1.66). Neither provides clean PGS-only AUC/R2, so the stronger disease-focused design plus stronger effect-size evidence favors PGS005217.

Both candidates target the same disease concept (trait_reported pancreatic cancer; trait_efo exocrine pancreatic carcinoma) and use the same sparse GWAS-hits construction (22 variants; genome-wide significant variants) with the same listed development cohorts, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is not a clean PRS comparator). Given that, PGS000083 has the cleaner endpoint ("Incident pancreatic cancer" vs PGS000663’s horizon-conditioned "0–10 years of follow-up" packaging) and shows slightly stronger effect-size evidence (HR per SD 1.49 vs OR 1.44) plus higher reported full-model discrimination (AUROC 0.745 vs 0.67), while PGS000663 also includes more clinically/mediator-adjacent covariates (waist-to-hip ratio, diabetic status, fasting status, blood collection timing) that make its full-model AUROC less interpretable for PRS quality. Validation size favors PGS000083 as well (391,491 vs 956), but this is secondary.

Both candidates align to Parkinson disease (same trait_reported/trait_efo), but PGS000903 has a cleaner generic disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: “Parkinson’s disease”) versus PGS003763’s incident-only framing (“Incident Parkinson Disease”), which is a mild endpoint restriction for a generic PD target. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², so we can’t use comparable PRS metrics; however PGS000903 provides stronger supportive discrimination evidence (OR top vs bottom quartile 6.25 and beta/SE) and comes from a large disease-focused GWAS meta-analysis with multiple development cohorts and multi-ancestry evaluation, whereas PGS003763 is a sparse 44-SNP genome-wide-significant score with only an HR tertile contrast (1.72) and no training/development details. Covariates are basic in both, so they don’t differentiate.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (same trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported), study context (same UKB portability paper), training size (n=391,124), covariates (basic demographics + PCs), and evaluation/ancestry distribution. With no PRS-only AUC/R2 for either, the main differentiators are the available PRS-comparable metric and structural properties: PGS002055 shows higher partial correlation (0.0175 vs 0.0151 for PGS001843) and is a genome-wide shrinkage score with far broader variant coverage (599,514 vs 242), which is generally favorable for a polygenic disease endpoint when other fields are matched.

Both candidates match the target well (trait_reported pancreatic cancer; trait_efo exocrine pancreatic carcinoma) and both are sparse 22-variant GWAS-hit style scores with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported, so full-model AUROC is not a clean differentiator. PGS000663 is better supported on endpoint/validation design: it is a disease-focused pancreatic cancer risk prediction study and shows broader evaluation ancestry (EAS 33%, EUR 67%) with multiple performance records (record_count=5), whereas PGS000794 is a pan-cancer risk-factor integration paper, evaluated only in EUR with a single record and includes explicit family history covariates that make its higher full-model AUROC (0.745) more likely covariate-driven and less comparable to standalone PRS performance. Effect sizes are similar (PGS000794 HR 1.49 vs PGS000663 OR 1.44), so the broader validation support and less framework-like packaging favor PGS000663.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all Parkinson’s disease), same publication family, same basic covariates (PCs 1–5, age, sex), same training cohorts and training N, and the same validation sample size (n=999), so performance and structural signals dominate. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC is only weakly informative; still, PGS000903 shows higher AUROC (0.692 vs 0.651) and additionally reports variance explained (R²=0.054) plus strong effect-size evidence (beta and OR top vs bottom quartile=6.25), whereas PGS000902 lacks these supporting metrics. Structurally, PGS000903 is a denser C+T score (1805 variants) versus a 90-variant GWAS-hits score, which is generally favorable for capturing polygenic signal when other fields are matched.

PGS005217 is better supported for the target peripheral vascular disease because it is a disease-focused PAD model with high endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported: incident peripheral artery disease; trait_efo: peripheral arterial disease—closely aligned to PVD) and provides meaningful PRS signal evidence via effect size (HR per SD 1.66) plus a reported C-index (0.731) with only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs). It is also developed/validated across many cohorts with broad multi-ancestry evaluation and a large validation sample (n=304,294), supporting transportability. In contrast, PGS001843 is from a UKB portability framework paper with a vague/unspecified phenotype (peripheral vascular disease, unspecified) and shows very weak PRS evidence (partial-r 0.0151) despite a larger training N; its sparse 242-variant construction and framework context provide less disease-specific support.

Both candidates align to the target trait (Parkinson disease) at trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS000902 has cleaner endpoint framing (phenotyping_reported: “Parkinson’s disease” vs PGS003763’s “Incident Parkinson Disease,” which is a narrower time-to-event endpoint). Neither reports PRS-comparable PGS-only AUC/R2, so performance can’t be compared on the preferred metrics; PGS000902’s AUROC=0.651 is explicitly a full-model metric and thus not a valid PRS-only advantage, while PGS003763 only reports an HR (1.72 high vs low tertile) which is also not directly comparable to PRS-only discrimination. With metrics essentially non-decisive, structural/study-support signals favor PGS000902: it is derived from a large, disease-focused multi-cohort PD GWAS meta-analysis (multiple PD consortia/cohorts listed) and uses more GWAS-significant variants (90 vs 44), whereas PGS003763 has no training sample/cohort details and appears embedded in a frailty-focused incident-PD analysis. Covariates are basic in both (PCs/array plus age/sex in PGS000902), with no obvious leakage. Overall, PGS000902 is better-supported on visible development context and endpoint generality.

PGS003586 is the better-supported match to the target trait preeclampsia: it has direct trait alignment (trait_reported = "Pre-eclampsia", trait_efo = preeclampsia) whereas PGS003587 is reported as "Gestational hypertension" despite sharing the same phenotyping_reported string. Both candidates are near-clones otherwise (same publication, method PRS-CS, training n=212,034, EUR-only development/evaluation, same basic covariates, same validation n=25,582, and no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported), so the main differentiator becomes endpoint fidelity and the available PRS signal proxy: PGS003586 also shows a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.31 vs 1.20 for PGS003587), supporting better discrimination within this sibling set.

PGS003587 is better supported for the target trait preeclampsia because its endpoint fidelity is stronger: despite the broader trait_reported label (“Gestational hypertension”), its phenotyping_reported is explicitly “Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia,” aligning directly with the target, whereas PGS004593 has an exact trait_reported (“Preeclampsia”) but phenotyping_reported is “Gestational hypertension,” a less faithful endpoint for preeclampsia. Both candidates lack PRS-comparable AUC/R2, so effect-size and study context matter more; PGS003587 reports a comparable per-SD OR=1.2 and comes from a disease-focused Nat Med multi-cohort development with listed training cohorts and a defined training N, while PGS004593 provides less development detail (samples_training N/A, no cohorts listed) and reports an HR=1.16. Covariates are basic in both, so they don’t differentiate strongly. Overall, the clearer preeclampsia phenotype anchoring and richer disease-focused development metadata favor PGS003587.

Both candidates are near-clones for the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all prostate cancer/prostate carcinoma), come from the same publication, have identical training cohort (UKB), training N (9,671), evaluation ancestry mix, covariates listed as 0, record_count (6), and validation sample size (171,474). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so the full-model AUROC/R² are only weak tie-breakers; nonetheless PGS004139 shows a trivially higher full-model AUROC (0.7003 vs 0.6994) and R² (0.1213 vs 0.1202) with essentially identical effect sizes (OR ~2.11). With no other differentiating evidence, PGS004139 edges PGS004042, but the margin is minimal, hence low confidence.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all prostate cancer/carcinoma), study context (same publication, UKB training n=9,671), ancestry distribution (EUR GWAS/DEV; EUR+SAS eval), covariates (0), and validation size (n=171,474), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model metrics, which are not ideal for PRS comparison). Given this near-tie, PGS004155 has consistently slightly stronger reported discrimination/effect evidence in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.7049 vs 0.7003; R² 0.1280 vs 0.1213; OR per SD 2.166 vs 2.109; β 0.773 vs 0.746) and also a higher variant count (1,139,693 vs 945,385), so it is better-supported on the visible fields than PGS004139.

PGS001287 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.67648; PGS R² 0.0335) with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array) and these are plausibly below the trait heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.0735). It also has clear training context (UKB; n=269,704) and a defined European validation record. In contrast, PGS000342 is disease-focused and label-aligned (psoriatic arthritis) but provides only a full-model AUROC (0.562) with unknown covariates and no PGS-only AUC/R², making its PRS signal hard to assess and likely weaker given the low discrimination. The main drawback for PGS001287 is its pan-trait framework origin ("813 traits" sparse snpnet), which lowers confidence, but the available PRS-only performance evidence still outweighs the sparse/unclear metric support in PGS000342.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all prostate cancer/prostate carcinoma), come from the same publication, have the same training cohort (UKB), training N (9,671), evaluation ancestry mix (EUR/SAS), validation N (171,474), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model metrics shown, so not ideal for PRS comparability). Given that, the best differentiator is the within-family empirical performance: PGS004155 shows slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.7049 vs 0.6994), higher R² (0.1280 vs 0.1202), and slightly stronger effect sizes (OR per SD 2.166 vs 2.112; β 0.773 vs 0.748) than PGS004042, with equally clean covariates (covariates=0). The advantage is modest and based on full-model metrics, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

PGS001313 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.6729 and PGS-only R²=0.04966 (with CIs for AUROC), whereas PGS002083 has no AUROC/R² and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0632), which is less directly comparable for PRS discrimination. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (psoriasis; PGS001313 is time-to-event but still psoriasis), and covariates are similarly basic (age/sex/PCs; no obvious clinical leakage). Although PGS002083 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many more variants and slightly broader evaluation ancestries, the lack of standard PRS-only metrics makes it less well-supported than PGS001313’s cleaner, directly interpretable PRS-only AUC/R² evidence.

Both candidates have clean endpoint alignment to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all psoriasis) and both are UKB-derived framework-style scores with only basic demographic/PC covariates (no obvious clinical leakage). The key differentiator is performance evidence: PGS001312 reports PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6916 and PGS-only R2=0.0523) on a European validation record, whereas PGS002083 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0632) and no PRS-only AUROC/R2, making cross-model PRS discrimination support weaker/less directly comparable. Although PGS002083 uses many more variants and a genome-wide shrinkage method (LDpred2) with larger training N, the absence of PRS-comparable AUC/R2 on the visible record leaves it less well-supported than PGS001312 for this head-to-head.

PGS001312 is the better-supported choice for the generic target trait psoriasis because it has higher PRS-comparable performance on the selected European validation (PGS-only AUROC 0.6916 and PGS-only R2 0.0523) than PGS001313 (PGS-only AUROC 0.6729; PGS-only R2 0.0497), with otherwise essentially identical study context (same pan-trait UKB framework paper, same training N=269,704, same covariates, same ancestry distribution, same validation N=67,425). Endpoint fidelity also favors PGS001312: its phenotyping_reported is direct 'Psoriasis', whereas PGS001313 is explicitly time-to-event ('TTE psoriasis' / 'Psoriasis (time-to-event)'), which is a mild mismatch for a generic disease-status target. Variant count is higher for PGS001313 (578 vs 204) but within this same-method sibling comparison the cleaner endpoint alignment plus better PRS-only metrics in PGS001312 outweigh that structural difference.

PGS001280 has cleaner, PRS-comparable performance reporting for pulmonary embolism: it provides explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.60765) and PGS-only R² (0.01403) with basic covariates disclosed, enabling a heritability-ceiling sanity check and avoiding reliance on covariate-driven full-model metrics. In contrast, PGS003861 matches the endpoint label well (Pulmonary embolism; EAS-focused disease study) but reports only a full-model AUROC (0.765) with unknown covariates and no PGS-only AUC/R², so its apparent discrimination is not comparable and could be largely covariate-driven. Despite PGS001280 being from a pan-trait UKB framework and using a time-to-event phenotype, the availability of PRS-only metrics and multi-ancestry evaluation support makes it better-supported on the visible fields than PGS003861’s metric-light record.

PGS001030 is better supported for the target trait (pulmonary fibrosis) because it provides PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.6252; PGS-only R2=0.0142) with basic covariates and has explicit training information (UKB, n=269,704) plus multi-ancestry evaluation records (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS), improving interpretability and transport context. In contrast, PGS004695 is endpoint-specific to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (incident IPF) and reports only an HR (high vs low quintile) without any PRS-only AUROC/R2, with no training sample details, making its standalone PRS performance harder to compare despite its large EUR validation (n=402,042).

PGS003586 is better supported for the target trait preeclampsia because its endpoint fidelity is direct (phenotyping_reported: “Pre-eclampsia/eclampsia”) and coherent with trait_reported/trait_efo, whereas PGS004593 has an explicit phenotype mismatch (phenotyping_reported: “Gestational hypertension”) despite the preeclampsia label. Both lack PRS-only AUC/R2, so effect-size and study context matter: PGS003586 shows a stronger per-SD association (OR 1.31 vs PGS004593 HR 1.16, suggesting weaker PRS signal) and provides clearer disease-focused multi-cohort development metadata (multiple named training/development cohorts and a stated training n=212,034), while PGS004593 has missing training/cohort details. PGS004593’s larger validation N does not outweigh the phenotype mismatch and weaker effect size.

Both candidates align well to the target (idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis) via trait_reported/trait_efo, but PGS001791 has cleaner PRS-comparable performance evidence: it reports a PGS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.005929 (and this is plausibly below the local h2_obs ceiling), whereas PGS004695 provides no PRS-only AUC/R2 and only a quintile HR (3.78) from an incident time-to-event framing. Structurally, PGS001791 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto) with ~910k variants and is developed across many biobanks, while PGS004695 is a sparse 23-SNP genome-wide-significant score from an exposure-focused study context, making it less supported as a standalone PRS despite the reported HR.

PGS001280 is the better-supported match to the target trait pulmonary embolism: its endpoint is explicitly PE with a time-to-event phenotyping (“TTE PE”) and trait_efo is pulmonary embolism only, whereas PGS001279 is a broader/less specific construct (“Blood clot in the lung”) and maps to a mixed trait_efo (pulmonary embolism, deep vein thrombosis), reducing endpoint fidelity. On PRS-comparable metrics, PGS001280 has higher PGS-only AUROC (0.60765 vs 0.60034) and higher PGS-only R² (0.01403 vs 0.01146), with both well below the heritability ceiling sanity check. Covariates, method (snpnet), training cohort (UKB), and ancestry distribution are essentially the same, so the decision rests on phenotype specificity and slightly stronger PRS-only performance in PGS001280; the larger validation N for PGS001279 is a weak tie-break and doesn’t outweigh these advantages.

PGS001137 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC=0.573 and PGS-only R2=0.00663 (no covariates), which are directly comparable and also pass the heritability sanity check (well below the local h2_obs ceiling ~0.004–0.005 on the observed scale, acknowledging scale differences but not showing an implausible exceedance). In contrast, PGS001833 provides no AUROC/R2 at all and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0218), which is less standard and harder to compare across models. Endpoint alignment is acceptable for both (both map to EFO retinal detachment; PGS001833 is slightly broader: 'detachments and defects'), and both are UKB-based framework/portability-style scores with basic covariates, so metrics availability/cleanliness is the main differentiator here.

PGS001030 is the better-supported choice for the target pulmonary fibrosis because it matches the umbrella endpoint directly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Pulmonary fibrosis”) and provides explicit PRS-only performance metrics (PGS AUROC 0.6252; PGS R2 0.0142). In contrast, PGS001791 targets the narrower subtype idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (not the full pulmonary fibrosis umbrella) and lacks a PRS-only AUROC (only a covariates-regressed-out R2=0.005929 is available), making its discrimination evidence weaker/comparability-limited. Although PGS001791 has a stronger structural setup (genome-wide PRS-CS-auto with many variants and multi-biobank development), the direct endpoint match plus clearer PRS-only metrics favor PGS001030 overall.

PGS001279 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.60034) and PGS-only R² (0.01146) with basic covariates listed, allowing a clean PRS contribution interpretation and a heritability-ceiling sanity check. In contrast, PGS003861 reports no PGS-only AUROC/R² and only a full-model AUROC (0.765), which the guidance says is not a valid substitute for PRS performance; its covariates are also unknown, further reducing comparability. While PGS003861 has exact pulmonary embolism endpoint fidelity and is disease-focused in Han Chinese (EAS), the lack of PRS-only metrics makes its apparent performance advantage non-comparable versus PGS001279’s explicit PRS-only metrics (despite PGS001279 being a pan-trait UKB framework score and having a broader trait_efo including DVT).

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/efo both rheumatoid arthritis; phenotyping_reported both Seropositive RA), covariates (both 0), training cohort (UKB), training size (n=820), ancestry distribution, and validation sample size (n=90,274), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (only full-model metrics, which are not ideal for PRS comparison). Given this tie on design/phenotype, PGS004049 has consistently stronger reported performance/effect evidence in the selected European validation record: higher AUROC (0.728 vs 0.719), higher R² (0.122 vs 0.113), and higher per-SD OR (2.37 vs 2.22). The differences are modest, so confidence is moderate rather than high.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = "Retinal detachments and defects"; trait_efo = retinal detachment), identical training cohort and size (UKB, n=391,124), identical covariates (basic demographics + PCs), identical ancestry distribution and validation sample size (n=19,445), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2. The main differentiators are (1) PRS-comparable performance proxy and (2) structural method/coverage: PGS002040 shows higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0276 vs 0.0218 for PGS001833) and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (706,872 vs 3,737), which is a positive structural signal when other fields are effectively tied. With no other conflicting evidence, PGS002040 is better supported than PGS001833.

PGS000922 is the better-supported choice for generic sarcoidosis because it has clean, PRS-comparable performance reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.64282; PGS-only R2=0.01741) with only basic covariates, and its phenotype fields are fully aligned (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all sarcoidosis). In contrast, PGS001872 has an endpoint mismatch in trait_efo ("skin sarcoidosis" vs target sarcoidosis) and lacks PRS-comparable AUC/R2 entirely (only partial correlation reported), making its predictive evidence less directly comparable despite more variants and larger training N.

Both candidates target rheumatoid arthritis with identical trait_reported/trait_efo and the same phenotyping_reported (Seropositive RA), come from the same publication, have the same training cohort (UKB), training size (n=820), ancestry distribution, covariates=0, and validation sample size (n=90,274), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R² (so full-model AUROC/R² are only weakly informative). Given this near-clone context, PGS004163 is better supported because it shows consistently stronger reported performance in the selected European validation record (full-model AUROC 0.7469 vs 0.7283; R² 0.1376 vs 0.1220; OR 2.46 vs 2.37) and it uses an ensemble/multi-score approach (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) versus the single-score LDpred2.CV in PGS004049, which is a positive structural signal when endpoints/covariates are otherwise identical.

Both candidates map to the target (trait_efo=retinal detachment) and have similar basic covariate adjustment without obvious clinical leakage. However, PGS001137 provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.573 and PGS-only R2=0.00663), which can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0042; same order of magnitude). In contrast, PGS002040 reports no AUROC/R2 and only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0276), which is less directly comparable as a PRS discrimination metric. While PGS002040 has a much larger variant count and training N, the lack of PRS-comparable AUC/R2 evidence makes it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001137.

PGS000923 is the better-supported sarcoidosis PRS on the visible fields because it has clear endpoint alignment (trait_efo=sarcoidosis; phenotyping_reported=TTE sarcoidosis) and, critically, reports PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64561 and PGS-only R2=0.018), which can be sanity-checked against the provided heritability ceiling. In contrast, PGS001872 has a notable phenotype mapping mismatch (trait_efo=skin sarcoidosis vs target sarcoidosis) and lacks PRS-comparable AUROC/R2 entirely, offering only partial correlation (partial-r=0.0199), making its predictive evidence less directly comparable. Both are UKB framework-style scores with basic covariates and similar multi-ancestry evaluation strings, so the decision is driven mainly by stronger phenotype match and cleaner PRS-only metric reporting for PGS000923.

Both candidates are near-clones on endpoint fidelity and study context: same trait_reported/trait_efo (rheumatoid arthritis), same phenotyping_reported (Seropositive RA), same covariates=0 (no covariate-leakage signal), same training cohort (UKB), same training n=820, same ancestry distribution and validation size (n=90,274). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot use PRS-comparable metrics and must treat the listed AUROC/R² as full-model and only weakly informative. Given that, PGS004163 has consistently stronger available performance/effect-size evidence than PGS004079 (higher full-model AUROC 0.747 vs 0.719; higher R² 0.138 vs 0.113; higher OR per SD 2.46 vs 2.22) and also a larger variant count (778,275 vs 402,214), aligning with the fallback tie-breakers when PGS-only metrics are absent.

Both candidates are near-clones: same target/endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all schizophrenia), same method (PRS-CS), same ancestry distribution (GWAS EAS+EUR; evaluation EUR only), and same basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, platform/batch), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported in either record (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Given that, PGS000136 has the stronger available performance/effect-size evidence: higher reported AUROC (0.64 vs 0.60) and higher OR per SD (1.7 vs 1.483) than PGS000134. PGS000134’s larger validation n (44,436 vs 18,461) is a weak tie-break and doesn’t outweigh the consistently stronger discrimination/effect size signals in PGS000136.

PGS000922 is the better match to the target trait as a generic sarcoidosis PRS: its trait_reported and phenotyping_reported are plain “Sarcoidosis,” whereas PGS000923 is explicitly a time-to-event (TTE) endpoint (“Sarcoidosis (time-to-event)”, phenotyping_reported “TTE sarcoidosis”), which is a mild endpoint-fidelity penalty for a generic disease-risk target. Both candidates come from the same pan-trait UKB framework paper, have identical training cohort/size, covariates (basic age/sex/PCs/array), ancestry distribution, and validation size, so those do not differentiate. Although PGS000923 has slightly higher PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.6456 vs 0.6428; PGS-only R2 0.018 vs 0.0174) and more variants (22 vs 12), the performance gap is small and does not outweigh the cleaner endpoint alignment of PGS000922. Both R2 values remain well below the liability h2 ceiling, so no heritability red flags apply.

Both candidates match the target endpoint equally well (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all align to carcinoma in situ of skin), use the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and share identical EUR-only training/evaluation context and sample sizes. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot use clean PRS-comparable metrics; we must rely on the available validation evidence. PGS000471 shows materially stronger reported discrimination and effect size in the selected validation record (full-model AUROC 0.569 vs 0.524; OR per SD 1.401 vs 1.09; top 1% vs rest OR 3.77 vs 1.48), suggesting a stronger PRS signal under comparable covariate adjustment. Although PGS000469 has a much larger variant count (PRS-CS genome-wide), its observed validation metrics are weaker here, so PGS000471 is better supported on the visible evidence.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sizes, and similarly basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported for either (so full-model AUROC is only a weak within-family signal). Given that, the best available discriminative evidence favors PGS000470: higher full-model AUROC (0.557 vs 0.524), higher Nagelkerke R² (0.0154 vs 0.00141), stronger per-SD OR (1.308 vs 1.09), and higher top-1% vs rest OR (2.45 vs 1.48). Although PGS000469 uses a genome-wide shrinkage method with many more variants, its observed validation metrics/effect sizes are consistently weaker here, so PGS000470 is better-supported on the visible record fields.

Both candidates are near-clones: same target trait/phenotyping (schizophrenia), same method (PRS-CS), same publication/date, same ancestry distribution (GWAS mostly EUR with small EAS; EUR-only evaluation), and same basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, platform/batch), with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported (only full-model AUROC, which is not a clean PRS-comparable metric). Given this near-tie, PGS000136 has the stronger visible performance signal (full-model AUROC 0.64 vs 0.60 for PGS000133, with overlapping but higher CI) and also a materially higher variant count (833,502 vs 604,645), which is a supportive within-method structural advantage. PGS000133’s larger validation n (33,694 vs 18,461) is only a weak tie-break and doesn’t outweigh the higher AUROC/variant-count evidence for PGS000136.

Both candidates are near-clones: same obstructive sleep apnea endpoint (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported match), same publication, same method family, same covariates (including BMI), same training cohorts (FinnGen/MGBB/MVP), same validation ancestry set and validation n=21,975, and both only report a full-model AUROC=0.79 (no PGS-only AUC/R2 to cleanly compare PRS performance). With metrics otherwise non-discriminating, the main differentiator is effect size: PGS005219 reports a materially stronger per-SD OR=1.98 (1.74–2.24) versus PGS005220 OR=1.53 (1.39–1.68), indicating stronger PRS signal. The AdjustedBMI vs UnadjustedBMI label difference does not change endpoint fidelity here given identical phenotyping and covariate lists, so PGS005219 is better-supported on visible PRS-relevant evidence.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Squamous cell carcinoma”), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), same training cohort (MGI) and same validation N (8,473), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). Given this near-clone setup, PGS000461 has slightly stronger overall performance signals (higher full-model AUROC 0.599 vs 0.593; higher Nagelkerke R² 0.0304 vs 0.0268; slightly higher per-SD OR 1.491 vs 1.448), while PGS000463’s only edge is a marginally higher top-1% OR (3.74 vs 3.51). With no PRS-only metrics to cleanly separate them, the small but consistent advantage across multiple reported metrics favors PGS000461.

Both candidates are near-clones: same schizophrenia endpoint (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all schizophrenia), same method (PRS-CS), same ancestry distribution (GWAS EAS+EUR; EUR-only evaluation), same covariates (age, sex, PCs, platform/batch), and both only report a full-model AUROC=0.6 (no PGS-only AUC/R2), so discrimination evidence is not cleanly comparable. With metrics essentially tied, the main differentiator is effect size: PGS000133 reports a stronger per-SD OR (1.691) than PGS000134 (1.483), which is the more informative PRS signal here than small AUROC CI differences or variant count. PGS000134 has more variants and a larger validation n, but those are weaker tie-breakers given identical endpoint/covariate context and absent PRS-only metrics.

Both candidates are near-clones: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (squamous cell carcinoma), same publication, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training/validation sample sizes, and same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so full-model AUROC differences are only weakly informative. Given that, PGS000461 has slightly stronger overall discrimination evidence (higher full-model AUROC 0.599 vs 0.589; slightly higher per-SD OR 1.491 vs 1.457 and higher pseudo-R² 0.0304 vs 0.0282) and also includes more variants (13 vs 10) within the same GWAS-hits method family. PGS000465’s higher top-1% vs rest OR (4.54 vs 3.51) is supportive but less central than the per-SD effect size and the small AUROC/R² edge favoring PGS000461.

PGS005220 is better supported for the target trait (sleep apnea) because it targets the clinically dominant subtype obstructive sleep apnea (trait_efo/phenotyping_reported both OSA), comes from a disease-focused multi-cohort development context (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP) with multi-ancestry evaluation, and shows a much stronger PRS signal via effect size (OR per SD 1.53) than PGS003213 (OR 1.106). Although both candidates only report full-model AUROC (not PRS-only) and thus AUROC is not cleanly comparable, PGS003213 is from the ExPRSweb framework repository (a known weaker archetype) and its AUROC is near-null (0.527), providing limited evidence of meaningful PRS discrimination. PGS005220’s inclusion of BMI as a covariate and its ‘UnadjustedBMI’ labeling reduce metric comparability, but the stronger disease-focused evidence package and effect size still outweigh the framework score’s exact umbrella label.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match carcinoma in situ of skin), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), identical covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), same training cohort (MGI) and same validation size (n=5,500), and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative). PGS005219 is better supported for the target trait (sleep apnea) because its endpoint is a clinically dominant subtype match (obstructive sleep apnea) with coherent phenotyping_reported, and it comes from a disease-focused multi-cohort development context (FinnGen, MGBB, MVP) with multi-ancestry evaluation. Although PGS005219 includes BMI adjustment (AdjustedBMI; covariates include BMI), that mild mediator adjustment is outweighed by its stronger disease-focused evidence package; PGS003213 is from the ExPRSweb framework-style repository with weaker discrimination and EUR-only development/evaluation.

Both candidates are near-clones for endpoint fidelity and study context: identical trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (squamous cell carcinoma), same publication, same EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL ancestry, same training cohort (MGI) and training n=8,029, same covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and same validation n=8,473. Both candidates are near-clones for the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match thyroid cancer/carcinoma), use the same GWAS Hits method with 10 variants, and have similarly clean/basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4) with no PRS-only AUC/R2 reported—so full-model AUROC is only weakly informative. Given that, PGS000631 has slightly stronger reported validation signals (higher full-model AUROC 0.636 vs 0.626; higher pseudo-R² 0.0478 vs 0.0393; higher top-1% OR 4.4 vs 3.53; slightly higher per-SD OR 1.651 vs 1.598), while PGS000630’s main advantage is larger training/validation size and mixed-ancestry evaluation (EUR+MAE), which are weak tie-breakers here. The evidence edge is small, hence low confidence.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all T1D), identical covariates (0), same training cohort (UKB) and training N (804), and the same ancestry distribution and validation size, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so full-model AUROC/R² are only weakly informative). Given this near-clone setting, PGS004162 is better supported by slightly stronger reported performance/effect evidence in the selected European validation record (higher AUROC 0.771 vs 0.758; higher R² 0.141 vs 0.124; higher OR per SD 2.89 vs 2.68) and a modestly higher variant count (62,645 vs 56,288), consistent with its ensemble MultiPRS structure versus the single-method megaprs score in PGS004078.

Both candidates are essentially endpoint-identical for the target (trait_efo thyroid carcinoma; trait_reported/phenotyping_reported thyroid cancer), from the same publication, with the same basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4) and EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL—so phenotype fidelity and transportability do not differentiate them. Neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2, so we cannot use clean PRS-comparable metrics; we must rely on the available full-model metrics/effect sizes as weak within-family signals. Because the metrics are full-model and differences are modest, confidence remains low.

Both candidates align well to the target (trait_efo type 1 diabetes mellitus; phenotyping_reported is T1D/Type 1 diabetes). However, PGS001297 provides clean PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.77118 and PGS-only R2=0.0912, with incremental AUROC reported) under only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs, array), and its PRS-only R2 is plausible under the provided liability h2 ceiling. Therefore PGS001297 is better-supported on the visible record fields.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity to thyroid carcinoma (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all “Thyroid cancer”), identical training cohort and size (MGI; n=4,481), identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1–4), and the same validation sample size (n=4,270). PGS000630 has slightly higher full-model AUROC (0.626 vs 0.618) and pseudo-R² (0.0393 vs 0.0365) and slightly higher per-SD OR (1.598 vs 1.568), while PGS000632’s main advantage is a higher top-1% vs rest OR (5.14 vs 3.53). With near-tied evidence and no PRS-only metrics, the small but consistent edge across AUROC/R² and per-SD OR favors PGS000630, though confidence is low.

Both candidates match the target endpoint well (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are T1D for both). The key differentiator is PRS-comparable performance evidence: PGS001297 reports explicit PGS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.77118; PGS-only R2=0.0912) with basic covariates, giving clean, comparable PRS signal, and its R2 is plausible under the provided liability h2 ceiling. In contrast, PGS004162 provides only full-model AUROC/R2 (0.771/0.141) with covariates listed as ‘0’ but no PGS-only AUC/R2, so its discrimination cannot be attributed to the PRS alone per the policy guidance. Although PGS004162 has a strong OR per SD (~2.89) and an ensemble-style method with many variants, the lack of PRS-only metrics makes it less well-supported on the visible fields than PGS001297.

Both candidates have exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ulcerative colitis) and similarly basic covariates without obvious clinical leakage. The key differentiator is performance comparability: PGS001306 reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.63006; PGS-only R2=0.02036), which are directly usable and sit plausibly below the provided heritability ceiling (h2_liability≈0.2646). In contrast, PGS001855 provides only a partial correlation (partial-r=0.0625) and no PRS-comparable AUROC/R2, making its predictive evidence less directly interpretable for PRS ranking despite higher variant count and larger training N. Therefore PGS001306 is better-supported on visible, PRS-comparable performance evidence.

Both candidates match the target endpoint well (trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are Type 2 diabetes) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², so the visible AUROC/R² are full-model and not directly comparable as PRS metrics. PGS002308 is better supported as a standalone PRS because it comes from a disease-focused trans-ancestry T2D PRS development/validation study with broad multi-ancestry evaluation (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/GME) and shows a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.96 vs 1.67 for PGS004152), which is a meaningful proxy for PRS discriminative power when PRS-only metrics are absent. PGS004152 has a larger validation N and an ensemble-style method label, but it is trained/developed in UKB EUR only and provides no covariate details beyond '0', while its weaker OR suggests less PRS signal; its full-model AUROC (0.64) also does not compensate given non-comparability. Overall evidence favors PGS002308.

Both candidates map cleanly to the target trait (trait_reported/type 2 diabetes; trait_efo/type 2 diabetes mellitus). However, PGS001781’s phenotyping is explicitly "Incident type 2 diabetes" (a narrower endpoint than generic T2D), and its very high reported AUROC=0.852 is only a full-model metric with multiple covariates (YOB, sex, PCs, batch, array), with no PRS-only AUC/R2—so that AUROC is not comparable evidence of standalone PRS quality. PGS004152 also lacks PRS-only metrics, but it has cleaner/empty covariates ("0"), a strong per-SD effect size (OR≈1.67 vs 1.52), and comes from an explicit multi-biobank evaluation/ensemble context with some non-EUR evaluation representation, making its evidence package less likely to be covariate-driven and more directly interpretable for PRS performance than PGS001781’s covariate-boosted AUROC.

Both candidates match the target trait well at the concept level (trait_reported and trait_efo are T2D) and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R², so the higher full-model AUROC in PGS001781 (0.852 vs 0.793) is not a reliable PRS-comparable differentiator. Endpoint fidelity slightly favors PGS002308 because its phenotyping_reported is generic “Type 2 diabetes” (closer to the generic target) whereas PGS001781 is explicitly “Incident type 2 diabetes,” which is a narrower time-to-event framing. Structurally, PGS002308 is a trans-ancestry PRS-CSx score with broader GWAS ancestry inputs and much broader evaluation ancestry coverage (AFR/AMR/EAS/EUR/GME) than PGS001781’s EUR-only GWAS, supporting better transportability for diverse populations. PGS002308 also shows a stronger per-SD effect size (OR 1.96 vs 1.52), which is meaningful evidence of PRS discriminative signal when PRS-only metrics are absent. Overall, PGS002308 is better-supported for general T2D risk across ancestries; confidence is moderate because both rely on full-model metrics and lack PRS-only performance reporting.

Both candidates are near-clones: same trait_reported/trait_efo (bladder cancer / urinary bladder carcinoma), same phenotyping_reported (Cancer of bladder), same method (GWAS Hits), same variant count (13), same EUR-only ancestry, and similarly basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4). PGS001250 is better supported on PRS-comparable performance evidence and endpoint specificity: it reports explicit PGS-only AUROC (0.5668) and PGS-only R² (0.00592) for a closely aligned kidney/ureter stone phenotype (TTE calculus of kidney and ureter), whereas PGS001864 provides only a weak partial correlation (partial-r=0.0323) and no PRS-only AUROC/R². Although both are UKB framework-style scores and PGS001864 has more variants and broader listed evaluation ancestries, the lack of comparable PRS-only metrics for PGS001864 makes its predictive strength harder to substantiate than PGS001250’s directly reported PRS-only discrimination.

PGS002075 is the better-supported choice for the target trait urolithiasis because its endpoint is a direct, generic diagnosis-style phenotype (“Urinary calculus” / urolithiasis) without time-to-event packaging, and it is evaluated across a broader set of ancestries (AFR/EAS/EUR/GME/SAS) consistent with a portability-focused design. Although PGS001250 reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC 0.5668; PGS R2 0.00592), it comes from the pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) and uses a time-to-event phenotype (“TTE calculus of kidney and ureter”), which is a noted endpoint-fidelity warning for a generic urolithiasis target. Given PGS002075’s cleaner phenotype alignment and broader evaluation context versus PGS001250’s framework/TTE drawbacks (despite having metrics), PGS002075 is preferred.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported = "Urinary calculus", trait_efo = urolithiasis), identical covariates (basic demographics + PCs), identical training cohort/size (UKB; n=391,124), identical ancestry distribution and validation sample size (n=19,913), and both lack PRS-only AUC/R2. The main differentiators are (1) comparable PRS metric: PGS002075 has higher partial correlation (partial-r 0.0385 vs 0.0323 for PGS001864), and (2) structural method/coverage: PGS002075 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2) with far more variants (731,196 vs 5,599), which is generally favorable when other fields are tied. With no cleaner PRS-only metrics available, these two signals together favor PGS002075.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ulcerative colitis) and use only basic covariates (no obvious clinical-risk packaging). Confidence is moderate because neither record reports PGS-only AUROC/R2, and PGS004253’s AUROC=0.66 appears to be full-model rather than PRS-only.

Both candidates have identical endpoint fidelity (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all match bladder cancer), identical ancestry context (EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL), identical covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and the same training/validation cohorts and sizes. Both candidates have identical endpoint alignment (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all match bladder cancer), identical basic covariates (age, sex, batch, PCs 1-4), and EUR-only GWAS/DEV/EVAL, and neither reports PRS-only AUC/R2 (so the full-model AUROC ~0.57 is not a clean PRS comparator). With metrics essentially tied, structural/effect-size signals break the tie: PGS000613 uses P+T with slightly more variants (15 vs 13), has larger training (12,992 vs 7,469) and validation (13,530 vs 7,622), and shows a much stronger top-1% vs rest OR (2.91 vs 1.47, with PGS000610’s CI crossing 1). PGS003381 is better supported for the target concept of uterine cancer because its endpoint is the clinically dominant subtype (endometrial carcinoma) and it uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (lassosum; 529,365 variants) with basic covariates (age + PCs) and a large EUR validation sample (n=144,479). PGS000541 matches the umbrella label exactly (malignant neoplasm of uterus; EFO uterine cancer) but is a sparse GWAS-hits score (18 variants) from a repository-style paper with much weaker reported discrimination (full-model AUROC 0.576 vs 0.761) and smaller validation (n=6,987). Neither provides PRS-only AUC/R², so structural signals (endpoint dominance + genome-wide model) and the much stronger observed performance package favor PGS003381 despite the slightly narrower subtype label.

PGS001795 is the better-supported match to the target trait “uterine cancer” on the visible PRS-comparable evidence: it has exact endpoint alignment (trait_reported/phenotyping_reported both “Uterine cancer”, trait_efo uterine carcinoma) and reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out metric (pgs_only_r2 = 0.001948), whereas PGS003381 is for the dominant subtype (endometrial carcinoma) and provides only full-model metrics (AUROC 0.761, R² 0.11) that are not PRS-comparable and likely covariate-influenced. Although PGS003381’s subtype is clinically close and its covariates are basic, the lack of any PGS-only AUC/R² makes its apparent performance advantage non-comparable; PGS001795 also has broader multi-cohort development context listed, with similar EUR-only evaluation.

PGS000760 is better supported on PRS-relevant evidence despite both having poor endpoint fidelity in `phenotyping_reported`. Candidate A (PGS000738) has a clear phenotype mismatch (`phenotyping_reported`: "Red hair") and only reports a full-model pseudo R² (0.0386) with unknown covariates, which is not a clean PRS-only metric. Candidate B (PGS000760) also has a mismatched, treatment/setting-specific phenotype ("anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients"), but it at least provides a PRS-relevant effect size (HR=1.41 per SD, moderate signal) and uses only basic covariates (5 genotype PCs), with a documented large training set (n=408,959, UKB). With no PGS-only AUC/R² available for either, the stronger comparable evidence package (effect size + basic covariates) favors PGS000760.

PGS001795 is the better-supported uterine cancer PRS on PRS-comparable evidence and structural quality: it reports a PRS-only/covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2 (0.001948), which is directly comparable and stays below the provided uterine-cancer heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.0005; liability≈0.0116), whereas PGS000541 does not report any PGS-only AUC/R2 (only full-model AUROC=0.576 and pseudo-R2=0.0133, which are not PRS-comparable). Endpoint fidelity is acceptable for both (uterine cancer/uterine carcinoma vs malignant neoplasm of uterus), and covariates are similarly basic (age/sex/PCs/batch). Structurally, PGS001795 uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (PRS-CS-auto) with ~912k variants and is developed across many biobanks with large EUR evaluation (n=170,276), while PGS000541 is a sparse GWAS-hits score with 18 variants from UKB only and much smaller evaluation (n=6,987). Confidence is moderate because neither provides a clean PGS-only AUROC and PGS001795’s PRS-only R2 is small.

Both candidates match the target endpoint cleanly (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all ulcerative colitis) and use only basic covariates (age/sex/array/PCs), so phenotype and leakage concerns don’t separate them. PGS001306 has explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC 0.630 and PGS-only R2 0.02036, below the h2_liability ceiling) and broader multi-ancestry evaluation, but it is from a known pan-trait sparse UKB framework (“across 813 traits”) with a very small 179-variant snpnet model—an archetype that domain guidance flags as systematically less reliable externally. PGS004253 comes from a disease-focused UC study context and uses a genome-wide shrinkage approach (LDpred2-auto) with far broader variant coverage (744,575) plus a strong per-SD effect size (OR 1.84), which is meaningful PRS evidence even though only a full-model AUROC (0.66) is reported and thus not directly comparable. Net: the disease-focused, genome-wide score with strong OR evidence (PGS004253) is better-supported than the sparse framework score (PGS001306), though confidence is tempered by missing PGS-only AUC/R2 for PGS004253.

PGS001536 is better supported on PRS-comparable evidence: it reports explicit PGS-only metrics (AUROC=0.64193; PGS R²=0.01621) with clearly stated basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and has defined training (UKB; n=269,704) plus broader evaluation ancestries (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS, even though the selected record is EUR). In contrast, PGS000738 has a major endpoint/phenotype coherence problem for the target trait vitiligo: while trait_reported/efo are vitiligo, phenotyping_reported is 'Red hair', and it lacks PRS-only AUC/R² (only a pseudo R²/full-model-like metric is shown), with unknown covariates and no training sample details. Given the phenotype mismatch and weaker comparable metrics for PGS000738, PGS001536 is the stronger choice despite being a pan-trait UKB framework score and having a time-to-event framing.

PGS001536 is the better-supported vitiligo PRS because its endpoint is directly vitiligo (phenotyping_reported: "TTE vitiligo") and it reports PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC=0.64193; PGS-only R2=0.01621), which are below the vitiligo heritability ceiling (h2_obs≈0.174) and thus plausible. It also has broader evaluation ancestry (AFR/EAS/EUR/SAS) with a large validation sample (n=67,425) and only basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/array). In contrast, PGS000760 has a major phenotype mismatch: phenotyping_reported is "anti-PD-L1 induced hypothyroidism in cancer patients" (treatment-induced, different endpoint), provides no PRS AUC/R2 (only an HR=1.41 and a meta-analysis p-value), and is validated in a much smaller sample (n=1,584) limited to EUR—making it weak evidence for generic vitiligo risk prediction despite the trait_reported label.
